bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第187卷卷第一百八十七

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 187, juan one hundred eighty-seven
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 187

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三】 起屠維單閼正月，盡十月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 3] Beginning in the first month of the year Tuyu Danqie, ending in the tenth month, less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 3] Spanning from the first month of the year Tuyu Danqie through the tenth month—a period of less than one year.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，王世充悉取隋朝顯官、名士為太尉府官屬，杜淹、戴冑皆預焉。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day Renyin: Wang Shichong took all the eminent officials and celebrated scholars of the Sui dynasty to serve as staff in his Grand Marshal's Office; Du Yan and Dai Zhou were among them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, on the day Renyin, Wang Shichong enlisted all the Sui dynasty's prominent officials and renowned scholars as staff in his Grand Marshal's Office; Du Yan and Dai Zhou were both included.

sentences.zh: 冑，安陽人也。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou was a man of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou was a native of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 隋將軍王隆帥屯衛將軍張鎮周、都水少監蘇世長等以山南兵始至東都。

translations.literal: The Sui general Wang Long led the Palace Guard general Zhang Zhenzhou, the Director of Waterways Su Shichang, and others with troops from south of the mountains, newly arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui general Wang Long led the Palace Guard general Zhang Zhenzhou, the Director of Waterways Su Shichang, and others, bringing troops from the region south of the mountains to the Eastern Capital for the first time.

sentences.zh: 王世充專總朝政，事無大小，悉關太尉府；

translations.literal: Wang Shichong monopolized control of court affairs; matters great and small all passed through the Grand Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong had seized control of the government, and matters large and small all had to go through his Grand Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 台省監署，莫不闃然。

translations.literal: The offices of the Secretariat, Chancellery, and supervisory agencies were all deserted.
translations.idiomatic: The central ministries and supervisory offices stood utterly idle.

sentences.zh: 世充立三牌於府門外，一求文學才識堪濟時務者，一求武勇智略能摧鋒陷敵者，一求身有冤滯擁抑不申者。

translations.literal: Shichong set up three placards outside his office gate: one seeking men of literary learning and talent fit to serve the times; one seeking men of martial courage and strategic wisdom able to break the enemy's van and storm their lines; one seeking those who had suffered injustice and oppression with no means to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong posted three notices outside his headquarters: one calling for scholars of learning and ability who could help govern the age; one for warriors of courage and strategy who could smash the enemy vanguard; and one for anyone who had suffered wrongs and had no channel to seek redress.

sentences.zh: 於是上書陳事者日有數百，世充悉引見，躬自省覽，殷勤慰諭，人人自喜，以為言聽計從，然終無所施行。

translations.literal: Thereupon several hundred people a day submitted memorials stating their cases. Shichong received them all in audience, personally read through them, and earnestly comforted and instructed them. Each person rejoiced, thinking his words would be heeded and his plans followed—yet in the end nothing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon hundreds of people were submitting petitions each day. Shichong met them all in person, read their submissions himself, and spoke to them with warm encouragement. Everyone went away pleased, believing he would act on their advice—but in the end he implemented nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 下至士卒廝養，世充皆以甘言悅之，而實無恩施。

translations.literal: Down to common soldiers and stable hands, Shichong used sweet words to please them all, yet in fact granted no real kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Even down to ordinary soldiers and grooms, Shichong flattered everyone with pleasant words, yet never bestowed any real benefit.

sentences.zh: 隋馬軍總管獨孤武都為世充所親任，其從弟司隸大夫機與虞部郎楊恭慎、前勃海郡主簿孫師孝、步兵總管劉孝元、李儉、崔孝仁謀召唐兵，使孝仁說武都曰：「王公徒為兒女之態以悅下愚，而鄙隘貪忍，不顧親舊，豈能成大業哉！

translations.literal: The Sui cavalry commander-in-chief Dugu Wudu was trusted by Shichong. His younger cousin, the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Dugu Ji, together with the Bureau of Parks and Forests attendant Yang Gongjing, the former chief clerk of Bohai commandery Sun Shixiao, the infantry commander-in-chief Liu Xiaoyuan, Li Jian, and Cui Xiaoren plotted to summon Tang troops. They had Xiaoren persuade Wudu, saying: 'The prince merely puts on childish airs to please the foolish masses, yet he is base, narrow, greedy, and cruel, heedless of kin and old friends—how could he accomplish great undertakings!
translations.idiomatic: The Sui cavalry commander Dugu Wudu enjoyed Shichong's favor. His younger cousin Dugu Ji, a Director of the Imperial Secretariat, joined with Yang Gongjing of the Bureau of Parks, the former Bohai chief clerk Sun Shixiao, the infantry commander Liu Xiaoyuan, Li Jian, and Cui Xiaoren in a plot to bring in Tang forces. Xiaoren urged Wudu: 'Our prince only plays the fond parent to win over the ignorant, yet he is petty, greedy, and cruel and cares nothing for kin or old ties—how could such a man build a lasting realm?

sentences.zh: 圖識之文，應歸李氏，人皆知之。

translations.literal: The prophetic texts say the mandate belongs to the house of Li; everyone knows this.
translations.idiomatic: The omens and prophecies all point to the house of Li, as everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 唐起晉陽，奄有關內，兵不留行，英雄景附。

translations.literal: Tang rose from Jinyang, swiftly seized the lands within the passes, its armies marched without pause, and heroes flocked to it in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang rose at Jinyang, quickly took the Guanzhong region, and its armies swept forward without stopping while heroes gathered to its banner.

sentences.zh: 且坦懷待物，舉善責功，不念舊惡，據勝勢以爭天下，誰能敵之！

translations.literal: Moreover it treats others with open sincerity, promotes the good and assigns merit, does not dwell on old wrongs, and contends for the realm from a position of advantage—who can oppose it!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Tang is open-hearted toward others, rewards merit and talent, and does not cling to old grudges. Contending for the empire from such a position of strength, who could stand against it!

sentences.zh: 吾屬托身非所，坐待夷滅。

translations.literal: We have placed ourselves in the wrong master and sit waiting to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: We have cast our lot with the wrong side and can only sit by while we are wiped out.

sentences.zh: 今任管公兵近在新安，又吾之故人也，若遣間使召之，使夜造城下，吾曹共為內應，開門納之，事無不集矣。」

translations.literal: Now General Ren Guan's troops are near at Xinan, and he is also an old friend of ours. If we send a secret messenger to summon him, have him come to the walls by night, and we together act as insiders and open the gates to admit him, nothing will fail.'
translations.idiomatic: General Ren Guan's army is now close at Xinan, and he is an old acquaintance of ours. If we send a secret envoy to call him and have his men come to the walls by night, we can act together from within, open the gates, and admit them—the plan cannot fail.'

sentences.zh: 武都從之。

translations.literal: Wudu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu agreed to the plan.

sentences.zh: 事洩，世充皆殺之。

translations.literal: The plot leaked out, and Shichong had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Shichong had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 恭慎，達之子也。

translations.literal: Gongjing was the son of Yang Da.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjing was a son of Yang Da.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，命秦王世民出鎮長春宮。

translations.literal: On day Guimao, the Prince of Qin Shimin was ordered to go out and garrison Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guimao, the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, was ordered to take up command at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及攻魏州總管元寶藏，四旬不克。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji attacked Wei prefecture's commander-in-chief Yuan Baocang and could not take the city in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji besieged Yuan Baocang, the commander of Wei prefecture, but failed to capture it even after forty days.

sentences.zh: 魏徵往說之，丁未，寶藏舉州來降。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng went to persuade him; on day Dingwei, Baocang surrendered the entire prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng went to persuade him, and on the day Dingwei, Baocang surrendered the whole prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊午，淮安王神通擊宇文化及於魏縣，化及不能抗，東走聊城。

translations.literal: On day Wuwu, the Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong attacked Yuwen Huaji at Wei county. Huaji could not resist and fled east to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuwu, Prince Huai'an Li Shentong attacked Yuwen Huaji at Wei county. Huaji could not hold his ground and fled east to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 神通拔魏縣，斬獲二千餘人，引兵追化及至聊城，圍之。

translations.literal: Shentong took Wei county, killed and captured more than two thousand men, led his troops in pursuit of Huaji to Liaocheng, and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong captured Wei county, killing and capturing more than two thousand of the enemy, then pursued Huaji to Liaocheng and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以陳叔達為納言。

translations.literal: On day Jiazi, Chen Shuda was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi, Chen Shuda was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，李密所置伊州刺史張善相來降。

translations.literal: On day Bingyin, Zhang Shanxiang, whom Li Mi had installed as governor of Yi prefecture, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingyin, Zhang Shanxiang, the governor of Yi prefecture whom Li Mi had appointed, came over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 朱粲有眾二十萬，剽掠漢、淮之間，遷徙無常，攻破州縣，食其積粟未盡，復他適，將去，悉焚其餘資；

translations.literal: Zhu Can had an army of two hundred thousand. He raided between the Han and Huai rivers, moved without fixed abode, stormed prefectures and counties, and before the stored grain was consumed would move elsewhere; when about to depart he burned all remaining supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can commanded two hundred thousand men. He plundered the region between the Han and Huai rivers, shifting camp constantly. He overran prefectures and counties, and before the grain he had seized was gone he would move on; when he left, he burned everything that remained.

sentences.zh: 又不務稼穡，民餒死者如積。

translations.literal: He also paid no heed to farming, and the people who starved to death piled up like heaps.
translations.idiomatic: He paid no attention to agriculture, and the dead from starvation lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 粲無可復掠，軍中乏食，乃教士卒烹婦人、嬰兒□敢之，曰：「肉之美者無過於人，但使他國有人，何憂於餒！」

translations.literal: When Can had nothing left to plunder and his army lacked food, he taught his soldiers to boil women and infants and eat them, saying: 'No meat is finer than human flesh; as long as other states still have people, why worry about hunger!'
translations.idiomatic: When there was nothing left to loot and his army ran short of food, Can ordered his soldiers to boil women and infants and eat them, saying, 'No meat is finer than human flesh—as long as other lands still have people, why should we fear hunger!'

sentences.zh: 隋著作佐郎陸從典、通事舍人顏愍楚，謫官在南陽，粲初引為賓客，其後無食，闔家皆為所□敢。

translations.literal: The Sui Assistant Editor of Writings Lu Congdian and the Master of Ceremonies Yan Minchu, both demoted officials at Nanyang, were at first taken in by Can as guests; later, when there was no food, their entire families were eaten by him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congdian, an Assistant Editor of Writings under the Sui, and Yan Minchu, a Master of Ceremonies—both demoted officials at Nanyang—had first been received by Can as honored guests; later, when food ran out, their whole families were devoured.

sentences.zh: 愍楚，之推之子也。

translations.literal: Minchu was the son of Yan Zhitui.
translations.idiomatic: Minchu was a son of Yan Zhitui.

sentences.zh: 又稅諸城堡細弱以供軍食，諸城堡相帥叛之。

translations.literal: He also levied the weak and frail from the fortified settlements to supply his army with food, and the settlements one after another led each other in revolt against him.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized the weak from the fortified settlements to feed his troops, and the settlements rose against him one after another.

sentences.zh: 淮安土豪楊士林、田瓚起兵攻粲，諸州皆應之。

translations.literal: The Huai'an magnates Yang Shilin and Tian Zan raised troops to attack Can, and the various prefectures all responded.
translations.idiomatic: The local strongmen Yang Shilin and Tian Zan of Huai'an raised forces against Can, and prefectures throughout the region joined them.

sentences.zh: 粲與戰於淮源，大敗，帥餘眾數千奔菊潭。

translations.literal: Can fought them at Huaiyuan, suffered a great defeat, and led several thousand survivors in flight to Jutan.
translations.idiomatic: Can met them in battle at Huaiyuan, was routed, and fled with a few thousand survivors to Jutan.

sentences.zh: 士林家世蠻酋，隋末，士林為鷹揚府校尉，殺郡官而據其郡。

translations.literal: Shilin's family for generations were chieftains among the Man tribes. At the end of the Sui, Shilin was a captain in the Hawk-raising Guard, killed the prefectural officials, and seized the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Shilin family had long been chieftains among the southern tribes. At the end of the Sui, Shilin served as a captain in the Hawk-raising Guard, killed the prefectural officials, and took control of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 既逐朱粲，己巳，帥漢東四郡遣使詣信州總管廬江王瑗請降，詔以為顯州道行台。

translations.literal: After driving off Zhu Can, on day Jisi he led the four commanderies of Handong and sent an envoy to the commander of Xin prefecture, the Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan, to request surrender. An edict appointed him Regional Commander of the Xianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After driving off Zhu Can, on the day Jisi he led the four commanderies east of the Han and sent envoys to Prince Lujiang Li Yuan, commander of Xin prefecture, to submit. The court appointed him Regional Commander of the Xianzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 士林以瓚為長史。

translations.literal: Shilin made Zan his chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin appointed Tian Zan as his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 初，王世充既殺元、盧，慮人情未服，猶媚事皇泰主，禮甚謙敬。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Wang Shichong had killed Yuan and Lu, fearing that hearts were not yet won over, he still fawned on Emperor Gong of Sui, showing him extreme courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Shichong had killed Yuan and Lu, he feared the court had not yet accepted him and continued to court Emperor Gong of Sui with elaborate deference.

sentences.zh: 又請為劉太后假子，尊號曰聖感皇太后。

translations.literal: He also asked to become the adopted son of Empress Dowager Liu and gave her the honorific title Sagely and Responsive Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to be adopted as a son by Empress Dowager Liu and honored her with the title Sagely and Responsive Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 既而漸驕橫，嘗賜食於禁中，還家大吐，疑遇毒，自是不復朝謁。

translations.literal: Before long he grew arrogant. Once, after being given food in the palace, he returned home and vomited heavily, suspecting he had been poisoned; from then on he no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he grew arrogant. Once, after dining in the palace, he returned home and vomited violently, suspecting poison; from then on he stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主知其終不為臣，而力不能制，唯取內庫彩物大造幡花；

translations.literal: Emperor Gong knew he would never truly be his subject yet lacked the power to restrain him, and could only take colored goods from the inner treasury to make great quantities of banners and flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong knew Shichong would never truly be his subject but lacked the power to restrain him, and could only take silks from the inner treasury to make banners and floral offerings.

sentences.zh: 又出諸服玩，令僧散施貧乏以求福。

translations.literal: He also brought out various garments and curios and had monks distribute them to the poor to seek merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought out robes and valuables and had monks distribute them to the poor in hopes of gaining merit.

sentences.zh: 世充使其黨張績、董浚守章善、顯福二門，宮內雜物，毫釐不得出。

translations.literal: Shichong had his partisans Zhang Ji and Dong Jun guard the Zhangshan and Xianfu gates; not the smallest item from within the palace could be taken out.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong posted his followers Zhang Ji and Dong Jun at the Zhangshan and Xianfu gates so that not even the smallest item could leave the palace.

sentences.zh: 是月，世充使人獻印及劍。

translations.literal: That month Shichong sent men to present a seal and a sword.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shichong sent envoys to present a seal and a sword.

sentences.zh: 又言河水清，欲以耀眾，為己符瑞雲。

translations.literal: He also claimed the Yellow River had run clear, wishing to dazzle the masses and make it a portent of his own destiny.
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed that the Yellow River had run clear, hoping to impress the people and claim it as an omen of his destined rule.

sentences.zh: 上遣金紫光祿大夫武功靳孝謨安集邊郡，為梁師都所獲。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal from Wugong, Jin Xiaomo, to pacify the frontier commanderies, and he was captured by Liang Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Jin Xiaomo of Wugong, a Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, to pacify the frontier commanderies, but Liang Shidu captured him.

sentences.zh: 孝謨罵之極口，師都殺之。

translations.literal: Xiaomo cursed him to the utmost; Shidu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomo reviled him without restraint, and Shidu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔追賜爵武昌縣公，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the second month an edict posthumously granted him the title Duke of Wuchang county, with the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict posthumously ennobled him as Duke of Wuchang county with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 初定租、庸、調法，每丁租二石，絹二匹，綿三兩；

translations.literal: The laws for land tax, corvée, and the equal tax were first fixed: each adult male paid two piculs of grain in land tax, two bolts of silk, and three ounces of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: The land tax, corvée, and equal-tax system was established for the first time: each adult male owed two piculs of grain, two bolts of silk, and three ounces of cotton.

sentences.zh: 自茲以外，不得橫有調斂。

translations.literal: Beyond this, no arbitrary levies were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these fixed obligations, no additional exactions were allowed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔：「諸宗姓居官者在同列之上，未仕者免其徭役；

translations.literal: On day Bingxu an edict stated: 'Members of the imperial clan who hold office shall rank above others of the same grade; those not in office shall be exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingxu an edict declared: 'Members of the imperial clan who hold office shall take precedence over colleagues of equal rank; those not in office shall be exempt from labor service.

sentences.zh: 每州置宗師一人以攝總，別為團伍。」

translations.literal: In each prefecture one clan director shall be appointed to oversee them, and they shall be organized into separate companies.'
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture shall appoint one clan director to oversee them, and they shall be organized into separate companies.'

sentences.zh: 張俟德至涼，李軌召其群臣廷議曰：「唐天子，吾之從兄，今已正位京邑。

translations.literal: When Zhang Side arrived in Liang, Li Gui summoned his ministers to court deliberation and said: 'The Son of Heaven of Tang is my younger cousin by clan; he has now taken the throne in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Side reached Liang, Li Gui convened his ministers and said: 'The Tang emperor is my cousin, and he has now taken the throne in the capital.

sentences.zh: 一姓不可自爭天下，吾欲去帝號，受其官爵，可乎？」

translations.literal: One surname cannot contend with itself for the realm. I wish to abandon my imperial title and accept his offices and ranks—is this acceptable?'
translations.idiomatic: One family cannot fight itself for the empire. I wish to renounce my imperial title and accept offices and titles from him—what do you think?'

sentences.zh: 曹珍曰：「隋失其鹿，天下共逐之，稱王稱帝者，奚啻一人！

translations.literal: Cao Zhen said: 'When the Sui lost the deer, all under heaven chased it together; those who called themselves kings or emperors were more than one!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen replied: 'When the Sui lost the realm, everyone rushed to seize it; more than one man has called himself king or emperor!

sentences.zh: 唐帝關中，涼帝河右，固不相妨。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor rules Guanzhong, the Liang emperor rules Hexi—they do not interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor holds Guanzhong and you hold Hexi—they need not clash.

sentences.zh: 且已為天子，奈何復自貶黜！

translations.literal: Moreover, having already become Son of Heaven, how can you demote yourself again!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you are already emperor—how can you demote yourself again!

sentences.zh: 必欲以小事大，請依蕭察事魏故事。」

translations.literal: If you must take the lesser to serve the greater, please follow the precedent of Xiao Cha serving Wei.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on acknowledging a superior, follow the precedent of Xiao Cha's submission to the Northern Wei.'

sentences.zh: 軌從之。

translations.literal: Gui followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui accepted this counsel.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，軌遣其尚書左丞鄧曉入見，奉書稱「皇從弟大涼皇帝臣軌」而不受官爵。

translations.literal: On day Wuxu, Gui sent his Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Deng Xiao to have an audience, presenting a letter styled 'your imperial cousin, Emperor of Great Liang, your subject Gui,' and did not accept offices or ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuxu, Li Gui sent his Left Vice Director Deng Xiao to court with a letter addressing the emperor as 'your imperial cousin, Emperor of Great Liang, your subject Gui,' and refused to accept any Tang title or office.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，拘曉不遣，始議興師討之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, detained Xiao and would not send him back, and began to discuss raising troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, detained Xiao, and began planning a military campaign against Liang.

sentences.zh: 初，隋煬帝自征吐谷渾，吐谷渾可汗伏允以數千騎奔党項，煬帝立其質子順為主，使統餘眾，不果入而還。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Yang of Sui personally campaigned against the Tuyuhun, the Tuyuhun khan Fuyun fled with several thousand horsemen to the Tangut tribes. Emperor Yang installed his hostage son Shun as ruler and had him command the remaining people, but could not enter their lands and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yang of Sui campaigned personally against the Tuyuhun, the khan Fuyun fled with several thousand horsemen to the Tangut tribes. Yang installed Fuyun's hostage son Shun as ruler and ordered him to command the remnant tribes, but the expedition failed to penetrate their territory and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會中國喪亂，伏允復還收其故地。

translations.literal: When China fell into turmoil, Fuyun returned and recovered his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: When China fell into chaos, Fuyun returned and reconquered his former domains.

sentences.zh: 上受禪，順自江都還長安，上遣使與伏允連和，使擊李軌，許以順還之。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, Shun returned from Jiangdu to Chang'an. The emperor sent envoys to ally with Fuyun and had him attack Li Gui, promising to return Shun to him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang founder took the throne, Shun returned from Jiangdu to Chang'an. The emperor sent envoys to ally with Fuyun and urged him to attack Li Gui, promising to return Shun to him.

sentences.zh: 伏允喜，起兵擊軌，數遣使入貢請順，上遣之。

translations.literal: Fuyun rejoiced, raised troops to attack Gui, repeatedly sent envoys with tribute requesting Shun, and the emperor sent Shun to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun was delighted, marched against Li Gui, and repeatedly sent tribute missions asking for Shun's return; the emperor sent Shun to him.

sentences.zh: 閏月，朱粲遣使請降，詔以粲為楚王，聽自置官屬，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Zhu Can sent envoys requesting surrender. An edict appointed Can King of Chu, allowing him to appoint his own officials and act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Zhu Can sent envoys to submit. The court appointed him King of Chu, authorized him to appoint his own officials, and granted him discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及以珍貨誘海曲諸賊，賊帥王薄帥眾從之，與共守聊城。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji used precious goods to entice the bandits along the coastal bends. The bandit chief Wang Bo led his followers to join him, and together they defended Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji used treasure to win over the bandits along the coast. Their leader Wang Bo brought his men to join Huaji, and together they held Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 竇建德謂其群下曰：「吾為隋民，隋為吾君；

translations.literal: Dou Jiande said to his followers: 'I am a subject of the Sui; the Sui is my sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande told his followers: 'I am a subject of the Sui, and the Sui is my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今宇文化及弒逆，乃吾仇也，吾不可以不討！」

translations.literal: Now Yuwen Huaji has committed regicide—he is my enemy, and I cannot fail to punish him!'
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji has murdered his sovereign—he is my enemy, and I cannot leave him unpunished!'

sentences.zh: 乃引兵趣聊城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his troops toward Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched his army toward Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通攻聊城，化及糧盡，請降，神通不許。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huai'an Shentong attacked Liaocheng. Huaji's grain was exhausted and he requested surrender, but Shentong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong besieged Liaocheng. When Huaji's supplies ran out he asked to surrender, but Shentong refused.

sentences.zh: 安撫副使崔世幹勸神通許之，神通曰：「軍士暴露日久，賊食盡計窮，克在旦暮，吾當攻取以示國威，且散其玉帛以勞戰士；

translations.literal: The Vice Commissioner for Pacification Cui Shigan urged Shentong to accept. Shentong said: 'Our soldiers have been exposed to the elements for a long time. The rebels' food is gone and their plans exhausted; capture is imminent. I shall take the city by assault to display the state's might and distribute their jewels and silks to reward the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Commissioner for Pacification Cui Shigan urged Shentong to accept the surrender. Shentong replied: 'Our men have been in the field too long. The rebels are starving and at their wits' end—victory is at hand. I mean to storm the city to display imperial might and distribute their treasure to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 若受其降，將何以為軍賞乎！」

translations.literal: If I accept their surrender, with what shall I reward the army!'
translations.idiomatic: If I accept their surrender, what will I have left to reward the army with!'

sentences.zh: 世幹曰：「今建德方至，若化及未平，內外受敵，吾軍必敗。

translations.literal: Shigan said: 'Dou Jiande is now arriving. If Huaji is not subdued, we shall be attacked from within and without and our army will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shigan said: 'Dou Jiande is on his way. If Huaji is not settled before he arrives, we will be caught between two enemies and our army will surely be defeated.

sentences.zh: 夫不攻而下之，為功甚易，奈何貪其玉帛而不受乎！」

translations.literal: To take a city without fighting is the easiest achievement—why be greedy for their jewels and silks and refuse!'
translations.idiomatic: Taking the city without a fight would be the easiest victory—why let greed for their treasure keep you from accepting!'

sentences.zh: 神通怒，囚世幹於軍中。

translations.literal: Shentong was angry and imprisoned Shigan in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong flew into a rage and had Shigan imprisoned in the camp.

sentences.zh: 既而宇文士及自濟北饋之，化及軍稍振，遂復拒戰。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Shiji sent supplies from north of the Ji River, Huaji's army gradually revived, and they again resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Shiji sent supplies from north of the Ji River, Huaji's forces recovered somewhat, and they resumed fighting.

sentences.zh: 神通督兵攻之，貝州刺史趙君德攀堞先登，神通心害其功，收兵不戰。

translations.literal: Shentong directed his troops in the assault. Zhao Junde, prefect of Bei, climbed the parapet first and reached the top. Shentong, jealous of his achievement, withdrew his troops and ceased fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong pressed the assault. Zhao Junde, prefect of Bei, was first over the wall, but Shentong, resentful of another man's glory, pulled his troops back and stopped fighting.

sentences.zh: 君德大詬而下，遂不克。

translations.literal: Junde cursed him bitterly and came down; the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Junde cursed him furiously and climbed down, and the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 建德軍且至，神通引兵退。

translations.literal: Jiande's army was about to arrive, and Shentong led his troops in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiande's army approaching, Shentong withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 建德與化及連戰，大破之，化及復保聊城。

translations.literal: Jiande fought Huaji in successive battles and routed him greatly; Huaji again held Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande fought Huaji repeatedly and routed him; Huaji fell back to defend Liaocheng again.

sentences.zh: 建德縱兵四面急攻，王薄開門納之。

translations.literal: Jiande unleashed his troops in fierce assault from all four sides; Wang Bo opened the gates and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pressed the attack from all sides, and Wang Bo opened the gates to let him in.

sentences.zh: 建德入城，生擒化及，先謁隋蕭皇后，語皆稱臣，素服哭煬帝盡哀；

translations.literal: Jiande entered the city and captured Huaji alive. He first paid his respects to Empress Xiao of Sui, addressing her with the language of a subject, dressed in plain garb and wept for Emperor Yang with full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande entered the city and took Huaji alive. He first paid court to Empress Xiao of Sui, addressing her as a subject, dressed in mourning white, and wept for Emperor Yang with full grief.

sentences.zh: 收傳國璽及鹵簿儀仗，撫存隋之百官，然後執逆黨宇文智及、楊士覽、元武達、許弘仁、孟景，集隋官而斬之，梟首軍門之外。

translations.literal: He collected the imperial seal of transmission and the regalia and ceremonial guards, comforted and preserved the Sui officials, then seized the traitorous faction—Yuwen Zhiji, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, and Meng Jing—gathered the Sui officials, and beheaded them, displaying their heads outside the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the imperial seal and ceremonial regalia, reassured the Sui officials, then arrested the regicides Yuwen Zhiji, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, and Meng Jing. Before the assembled Sui court he had them beheaded and their heads displayed outside the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 以檻車載化及並二子承基、承趾至襄國，斬之。

translations.literal: He loaded Huaji and his two sons Chenggi and Chengzhi into caged carts, brought them to Xiangguo, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Huaji and his sons Chenggi and Chengzhi in caged carts, brought them to Xiangguo, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 化及且死，更無餘言，但云：「不負夏王！」

translations.literal: As Huaji was about to die he said nothing more, only: 'I have not failed King Xia!'
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Huaji said nothing else but: 'I have not failed King Xia!'

sentences.zh: 建德每戰勝克城，所得資財，悉以分將士，身無所取。

translations.literal: Whenever Jiande won battles and took cities, all goods obtained he distributed entirely among his officers and soldiers, taking nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jiande won a battle or captured a city, he divided all the spoils among his officers and men and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 又不□敢肉，常食蔬，茹粟飯；

translations.literal: He also did not eat meat, regularly eating vegetables and plain millet rice.
translations.idiomatic: He ate no meat, living chiefly on vegetables and plain millet.

sentences.zh: 妻曹氏，不衣紈綺，所役婢妾，才十許人。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Cao did not wear silk gauze or brocade, and the maids and concubines in her service numbered only about ten.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Cao wore no silk or brocade, and she kept only about ten maids and concubines.

sentences.zh: 及破化及，得隋宮人千數，即時散遣之。

translations.literal: When he defeated Huaji and obtained several thousand Sui palace women, he immediately dispersed and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Huaji he took charge of several thousand Sui palace women and immediately sent them all away.

sentences.zh: 以隋黃門侍郎裴矩為左僕射，掌選事，兵部侍郎崔君肅為侍中，少府令何稠為工部尚書，右司郎中柳調為左丞，虞世南為黃門侍郎，歐陽詢為太常卿。

translations.literal: He appointed the Sui Director of the Palace Secretariat Pei Ju as Left Vice Director, in charge of selection; the Vice Minister of War Cui Junsu as Palace Attendant; the Director of the Palace Workshops He Chou as Minister of Works; the Right Department Director Liu Diao as Left Assistant; Yu Shinan as Director of the Palace Secretariat; and Ouyang Xun as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Pei Ju, former Sui Director of the Palace Secretariat, as Left Vice Director in charge of appointments; Cui Junsu, Vice Minister of War, as Palace Attendant; He Chou, Director of the Palace Workshops, as Minister of Works; Liu Diao of the Right Department as Left Assistant; Yu Shinan as Director of the Palace Secretariat; and Ouyang Xun as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 詢，紇之子也。

translations.literal: Xun was the son of Ouyang He.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun was a son of Ouyang He.

sentences.zh: 自餘隨才授職，委以政事。

translations.literal: For the rest he assigned offices according to talent and entrusted them with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The others he appointed according to their abilities and entrusted with the administration.

sentences.zh: 其不願留，欲詣關中及東都者，亦聽之，仍給資糧，以兵援之出境。

translations.literal: Those who did not wish to remain and wished to go to Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital were also permitted to do so; he still provided supplies and grain and escorted them across the border with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to leave for Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital were allowed to go, and he supplied them with provisions and escorted them to the border with troops.

sentences.zh: 隋驍果尚近萬人，亦各縱遣，任其所之。

translations.literal: Nearly ten thousand of the Sui elite guard still remained; he also released them all and let them go where they would.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand of the Sui elite guard still remained, and he released them all to go wherever they chose.

sentences.zh: 又與王世充結好，遣使奉表於隋皇泰主，皇泰主封為夏王。

translations.literal: He also formed friendly ties with Wang Shichong, sent envoys with a memorial to Emperor Gong of Sui, and Emperor Gong enfeoffed him as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He also made peace with Wang Shichong, sent a memorial to Emperor Gong of Sui, and was enfeoffed as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 建德起於群盜，雖建國，未有文物法度，裴矩為之定朝儀，制律令，建德甚悅，每從之咨訪典禮。

translations.literal: Jiande had risen from banditry; although he had founded a state, he had no civil institutions or laws. Pei Ju fixed court ritual for him and drafted statutes and ordinances. Jiande was greatly pleased and constantly consulted him on ceremonial matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande had risen from banditry, and though he had founded a state he lacked proper institutions. Pei Ju established court ritual and drafted laws for him. Jiande was delighted and constantly sought his counsel on ceremony.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上考第群臣，以李綱、孫伏伽為第一。

translations.literal: On day Jiachen the emperor graded the ministers; Li Gang and Sun Fuga were ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiachen the emperor ranked his ministers in performance review, placing Li Gang and Sun Fuga at the top.

sentences.zh: 因置酒高會，謂裴寂等曰：「隋氏以主驕臣諂亡天下，朕即位以來，每虛心求諫，然唯李綱差盡忠款，孫伏伽可謂誠直。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set out wine for a grand feast and said to Pei Ji and others: 'The house of Sui perished the realm because the ruler was arrogant and ministers flattered; since I took the throne I have sought counsel with an open mind, yet only Li Gang has come close to full loyalty, and Sun Fuga may be called sincere and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a grand banquet and told Pei Ji and the others: 'The Sui lost the empire because its ruler grew arrogant and its ministers flattered him. Since my accession I have sought advice with an open mind, yet only Li Gang has shown real loyalty, and Sun Fuga may truly be called honest and forthright.

sentences.zh: 餘人猶踵敝風，俯眉而已，豈朕所望哉！

translations.literal: The rest still follow the old corrupt ways, merely lowering their brows—is this what I hope for!
translations.idiomatic: The rest still follow the old habit of bowing and scraping—is that what I expect of you!

sentences.zh: 朕視卿如愛子，卿當視朕如慈父。

translations.literal: I regard you as beloved sons; you should regard me as a loving father.
translations.idiomatic: I regard you as my own sons; you should regard me as a father.

sentences.zh: 有懷必盡，勿自隱也。」

translations.literal: Whatever is in your hearts you must speak fully—do not hide it.'
translations.idiomatic: Speak your minds fully and hold nothing back.'

sentences.zh: 因命捨君臣之敬，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: He then ordered them to set aside the formalities between ruler and minister and disbanded only after the utmost revelry.
translations.idiomatic: He then told them to set aside court formality, and the feast broke up only after everyone had drunk their fill.

sentences.zh: 遣前御史大夫段確使於朱粲。

translations.literal: He sent the former Censor-in-Chief Duan Que as envoy to Zhu Can.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the former Censor-in-Chief Duan Que as envoy to Zhu Can.

sentences.zh: 初，上為隋殿內少監，宇文士及為尚輦奉御，上與之善。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Deputy Director of the Palace Secretariat under the Sui, Yuwen Shiji was Master of the Imperial Carriages; the emperor was on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor served as Deputy Director of the Palace Secretariat under the Sui, Yuwen Shiji was Master of the Imperial Carriages, and the two were close friends.

sentences.zh: 士及從化及至黎陽，上手詔召之，士及潛遣家僮間道詣長安，又因使者獻金環。

translations.literal: Shiji followed Huaji to Liyang. The emperor sent a secret edict summoning him. Shiji secretly sent a household slave by a hidden route to Chang'an and also had an envoy present a gold ring.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji followed Huaji to Liyang. The emperor summoned him by secret edict. Shiji secretly sent a household slave by a back road to Chang'an and also sent a gold ring through an envoy.

sentences.zh: 化及至魏縣，兵勢日蹙，士及勸之歸唐，化及不從，內史令封德彝說士及於濟北征督軍糧以觀其變。

translations.literal: When Huaji reached Wei county his military situation grew daily more desperate. Shiji urged him to submit to Tang, but Huaji would not listen. The Director of the Secretariat Feng Deyi persuaded Shiji to go north of the Ji River to levy and supervise army grain so as to watch how events developed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji reached Wei county his position grew desperate day by day. Shiji urged him to surrender to the Tang, but Huaji refused. Feng Deyi, Director of the Secretariat, persuaded Shiji to go north of the Ji River to collect army provisions and watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 化及稱帝，立士及為蜀王。

translations.literal: When Huaji declared himself emperor he installed Shiji as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji declared himself emperor he made Shiji King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 化及死，士及與德彝自濟北來降。

translations.literal: When Huaji died, Shiji and Deyi came from north of the Ji River to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's death, Shiji and Deyi came from north of the Ji River to submit.

sentences.zh: 時士及妹為昭儀，由是授上儀同。

translations.literal: At that time Shiji's younger sister was a Senior Concubine, and for this reason he was granted the rank of Upper Companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji's younger sister was then a Senior Concubine, and for this reason he was granted the rank of Upper Companionship.

sentences.zh: 上以封德彝隋室舊臣，而諂巧不忠，深誚責之，罷遣就捨。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Feng Deyi was an old minister of the Sui house yet was flattering, crafty, and disloyal, rebuked him severely and dismissed him to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw Feng Deyi as a former Sui minister who was flattering and disloyal, rebuked him harshly, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 德彝以秘策幹上，上悅，尋拜內史舍人，俄遷待郎。

translations.literal: Deyi presented secret stratagems to win the emperor's favor; the emperor was pleased and soon appointed him Attendant of the Secretariat, then quickly promoted him to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi won the emperor over with secret counsel. The emperor was pleased and soon appointed him Attendant of the Secretariat, then quickly promoted him to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，隋夷陵郡丞安陸許紹帥黔安、武陵、澧陽等諸郡來降。

translations.literal: On day Jiayin, Xu Shao of Anlu, acting magistrate of Yiling commandery under the Sui, led the commanderies of Qian'an, Wuling, Liyang, and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiayin, Xu Shao of Anlu, acting magistrate of Yiling commandery, led Qian'an, Wuling, Liyang, and other commanderies in submission.

sentences.zh: 紹幼與帝同學；

translations.literal: Shao had studied with the emperor in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had been the emperor's schoolmate in youth.

sentences.zh: 詔以紹為峽州刺史，賜爵安陸公。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shao governor of Xia prefecture and enfeoffed him as Duke of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shao governor of Xia prefecture and enfeoffed him as Duke of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以徐世勣為黎州總管。

translations.literal: On day Bingchen, Xu Shiji was appointed commander of Li prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen, Xu Shiji was appointed commander of Li prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，驃騎將軍張孝鈱以勁卒百人襲王世充汜水城，入其郛，沉米船百五十艘。

translations.literal: On day Dingsi, the General of Flying Cavalry Zhang Xiaoyin with a hundred crack troops raided Wang Shichong's Sishui city, entered its outer wall, and sank one hundred fifty grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingsi, General of Flying Cavalry Zhang Xiaoyin led a hundred elite troops in a raid on Wang Shichong's Sishui city, entered the suburbs, and sank one hundred fifty grain transports.

sentences.zh: 己未，世充寇穀州。

translations.literal: On day Jiwei, Shichong raided Gu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiwei, Shichong attacked Gu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世充以秦叔寶為龍驤大將軍，程知節為將軍，待之皆厚。

translations.literal: Shichong appointed Qin Shubao Grand General of the Dragon Cavalry and Cheng Zhijie a general, treating both with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong appointed Qin Shubao Grand General of the Dragon Cavalry and Cheng Zhijie a general, treating both with great favor.

sentences.zh: 然二人疾世充多詐，知節謂叔寶曰：「王公器度淺狹而多妄語，好為咒誓，此乃老巫嫗耳，豈撥亂之主乎！」

translations.literal: Yet the two detested Shichong's deceitfulness. Zhijie said to Shubao: 'Our prince's capacity is shallow and narrow, and he speaks much falsehood, fond of oaths and curses—he is but an old witch, how could he be a ruler who settles chaos!'
translations.idiomatic: Yet both men despised Shichong's treachery. Zhijie said to Shubao: 'Our prince is petty and deceitful, forever swearing oaths like some old village witch—how could such a man pacify the realm!'

sentences.zh: 世充與唐兵戰於九曲，叔寶、知節皆將兵在陳，與其徒數十騎，西馳百許步，下馬拜世充曰：「僕荷公殊禮，深思報效；

translations.literal: Shichong fought Tang troops at Jiuqu. Shubao and Zhijie both commanded troops in the formation. With several dozen horsemen of their following they galloped west about a hundred paces, dismounted, and bowed to Shichong, saying: 'Your servant has received your exceptional favor and deeply wished to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong fought the Tang at Jiuqu, Shubao and Zhijie were both in the line. With several dozen followers they rode west about a hundred paces, dismounted, and bowed to Shichong: 'I have received exceptional favor from you and long wished to repay it.

sentences.zh: 公性猜忌，喜信讒言，非僕托身之所，今不能仰事，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: Your nature is suspicious and you delight in believing slander—this is no place for your servant to entrust himself. I can no longer serve you upward; I beg leave to part here.
translations.idiomatic: But you are suspicious by nature and quick to believe slander. This is no lord I can serve. I can remain no longer and beg leave to depart.'

sentences.zh: 遂躍馬來降，世充不敢逼。

translations.literal: Thereupon they leapt on their horses and came to surrender; Shichong did not dare pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: They then spurred their horses toward the Tang lines, and Shichong did not dare stop them.

sentences.zh: 上使事秦王世民，世民素聞其名，厚禮之，以叔寶為馬軍總管，知節為左三統軍。

translations.literal: The emperor had them serve the Prince of Qin Shimin. Shimin had long heard their names and treated them with great courtesy, appointing Shubao cavalry commander-in-chief and Zhijie Left Third Corps Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assigned them to Prince Qin Li Shimin, who had long admired their reputations and received them with great honor. He made Shubao cavalry commander and Zhijie Left Third Corps Commander.

sentences.zh: 時世充驍將又有驃騎武安李君羨、征南將軍臨邑田留安，亦惡世充之為人，帥眾來降。

translations.literal: At that time among Shichong's fierce generals were also the Flying Cavalryman of Wu'an Li Junxian and the General Who Pacifies the South Tian Liu'an of Linyi; they too detested Shichong's character and led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Two more of Shichong's fierce generals, Li Junxian of Wu'an and Tian Liu'an of Linyi, also despised Shichong's character and came over with their men.

sentences.zh: 世民引君羨置左右，以留安為右四統軍。

translations.literal: Shimin kept Junxian at his side and appointed Liu'an Right Fourth Corps Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin kept Junxian at his side and made Liu'an Right Fourth Corps Commander.

sentences.zh: 王世充囚李育德之兄厚德於獲嘉，厚德與其守將趙君穎逐殷州刺史段大師，以城來降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong imprisoned Li Yude's elder brother Houde at Huojia. Houde, together with the defending general Zhao Junying, drove out Yin prefecture's governor Duan Dashi and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong had imprisoned Li Yude's elder brother Houde at Huojia. Houde joined the garrison commander Zhao Junying in expelling Yin prefecture's governor Duan Dashi and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 以厚德為殷州刺史。

translations.literal: Houde was appointed governor of Yin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Houde was appointed governor of Yin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 竇建德陷邢州，執總管陳君賓。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande took Xing prefecture and seized the commander Chen Junbin.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande captured Xing prefecture and seized its commander Chen Junbin.

sentences.zh: 上遣殿內監竇誕、右衛將軍宇文歆助并州總管齊王元吉守晉陽。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Palace Director Dou Dan and the Right Guard general Yuwen Xin to assist the Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, commander of Bing prefecture, in defending Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Director Dou Dan and Right Guard general Yuwen Xin to help Prince Qi Li Yuanji, commander of Bing prefecture, defend Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 誕，抗之子也，尚帝女襄陽公主。

translations.literal: Dan was the son of Dou Kang and had married the emperor's daughter, Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a son of Dou Kang and had married the emperor's daughter, Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 元吉性驕侈，奴客婢妾數百人，好使之被甲，戲為攻戰，前後死傷甚眾，元吉亦嘗被傷。

translations.literal: Yuanji's nature was arrogant and extravagant. He had several hundred male and female servants and concubines and liked to have them don armor and play at attack and battle; before and after, many were killed or wounded, and Yuanji himself was once injured.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was arrogant and extravagant. He kept several hundred servants and concubines and liked to arm them for mock battles; many were killed or wounded, and Yuanji himself was once hurt.

sentences.zh: 其乳母陳善意苦諫，元吉醉，怒，命壯士毆殺之。

translations.literal: His wet nurse Chen Shanyi remonstrated bitterly. Yuanji, drunk, grew angry and ordered strong men to beat her to death.
translations.idiomatic: His wet nurse Chen Shanyi pleaded with him repeatedly. Drunk and enraged, Yuanji ordered his men to beat her to death.

sentences.zh: 性好田獵，載罔罟三十餘車，嘗言：「我寧三日不食，不能一日不獵。」

translations.literal: He loved hunting in the fields and loaded more than thirty cartloads of nets and snares, once saying: 'I would rather go three days without eating than one day without hunting.'
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting and traveled with more than thirty cartloads of nets and snares, saying once, 'I would rather go three days without food than one day without the hunt.'

sentences.zh: 常與誕遊獵，蹂踐人禾稼。

translations.literal: He often went hunting with Dan, trampling people's grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: He often hunted with Dan, trampling the farmers' crops.

sentences.zh: 又縱左右奪民物，當衢射人，觀其避箭。

translations.literal: He also let his attendants seize people's goods, shot at people in the middle of the street, and watched them dodge the arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He let his followers rob the people, shot at passersby in the streets, and amused himself watching them dodge.

sentences.zh: 夜，開府門，宣淫他室。

translations.literal: At night he opened the mansion gates and forced himself on women in other households.
translations.idiomatic: At night he opened his mansion gates and violated women in other households.

sentences.zh: 百姓憤怨，歆屢諫不納，乃表言其狀。

translations.literal: The people were furious and resentful. Xin repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded, and so submitted a memorial describing his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed with anger. Xin remonstrated repeatedly without effect and finally memorialized the throne describing Yuanji's conduct.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，元吉坐免官。

translations.literal: On day Renxu, Yuanji was removed from office for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renxu, Yuanji was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，陟州刺史李育德攻下王世充河內堡聚三十一所。

translations.literal: On day Guihai, Li Yude, governor of Zhi prefecture, captured thirty-one of Wang Shichong's fortified clusters in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guihai, Li Yude, governor of Zhi prefecture, captured thirty-one of Wang Shichong's fortified posts in Henei.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，世充遣其兄子君廓侵陟州，李育德擊走之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On day Yichou, Shichong sent his elder brother's son Junguo to raid Zhi prefecture. Li Yude attacked and drove him off, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou, Shichong sent his nephew Junguo to raid Zhi prefecture. Li Yude repulsed him and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 李厚德歸省親疾，使李育德守獲嘉，世充並兵攻之，丁卯，城陷，育德及弟三人皆戰死。

translations.literal: Li Houde returned home to visit his parents' illness and left Li Yude to defend Huojia. Shichong concentrated troops to attack it. On day Dingmao the city fell; Yude and his three younger brothers all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Houde went home to tend his parents' illness and left Yude to hold Huojia. Shichong concentrated his forces against the city. On the day Dingmao it fell, and Yude and his three brothers all died fighting.

sentences.zh: 己巳，李公逸以雍丘來降，拜杞州總管，以其族弟善行為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: On day Jisi, Li Gongyi surrendered Yongqiu. He was appointed commander of Qi prefecture, and his clansman younger brother Shanxing was made governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jisi, Li Gongyi surrendered Yongqiu. He was appointed commander of Qi prefecture, and his cousin Shanxing was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 隋吏部侍郎楊恭仁，從宇文化及至河北；

translations.literal: Yang Gongren, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel under the Sui, had followed Yuwen Huaji to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren, former Sui Vice Minister of Personnel, had followed Yuwen Huaji to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，魏州總管元寶藏獲之，己巳，送長安。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, Yuan Baocang, commander of Wei prefecture, captured him. On day Jisi he was sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was defeated, Yuan Baocang, commander of Wei prefecture, captured him and on the day Jisi sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上與之有舊，拜黃門侍郎，尋以為涼州總管。

translations.literal: The emperor had old ties with him and appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, then soon made him commander of Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew him from old days, appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, and soon made him commander of Liang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 恭仁素習邊事，曉羌、胡情偽，民夷悅服，自蔥嶺已東，並入朝貢。

translations.literal: Gongren was versed in frontier affairs from of old and understood the true and false among the Qiang and Hu peoples. Chinese and barbarians alike were pleased to submit; from east of the Onion Mountains all came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren had long experience on the frontier and understood the Qiang and Hu peoples. Chinese and tribesmen alike submitted willingly, and from east of the Onion Mountains all sent tribute to court.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢可汗將其眾渡河至夏州，梁師都發兵會之，以五百騎授劉武周，欲自句注入寇太原。

translations.literal: The Türk qaghan Shibi led his masses across the river to Xia prefecture. Liang Shidu sent troops to join him and gave five hundred horsemen to Liu Wuzhou, intending to invade Taiyuan from Gouzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk qaghan Shibi led his people across the river to Xia prefecture. Liang Shidu sent troops to join him and gave Liu Wuzhou five hundred horsemen, planning to invade Taiyuan from Gouzhu.

sentences.zh: 會始畢卒，子什缽苾幼，未可立，立其弟俟利弗設為處羅可汗。

translations.literal: Just then Shibi died. His son Shibole was young and could not yet be enthroned, so his younger brother Tolifu was installed as Qaghan Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi then died. His son Shibole was still a child and could not succeed, so his younger brother Tolifu was installed as Qaghan Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 處羅以什缽苾為尼步設，使居東偏，直幽州之北。

translations.literal: Chuluo made Shibole the Eastern Qaghan and had him dwell in the eastern sector, directly north of You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo made Shibole the Eastern Qaghan and stationed him in the east, directly north of You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，上遣右武候將軍高靜奉幣使於始畢，至豐州，聞始畢卒，敕納於所在之庫。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent the Right Martial Guard general Gao Jing with tribute as envoy to Shibi. When he reached Feng prefecture he heard that Shibi had died and was ordered to deposit the gifts in the local treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent Right Martial Guard general Gao Jing with tribute to Shibi. At Feng prefecture he learned of Shibi's death and was ordered to deposit the gifts in the local treasury.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞之，怒，欲入寇；

translations.literal: When the Türks heard this they were angry and wished to invade.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türks heard of this they were furious and prepared to raid.

sentences.zh: 豐州總管張長遜遣高靜以幣出塞為朝廷致賻，突厥乃還。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsun, commander of Feng prefecture, sent Gao Jing with the tribute beyond the border to present condolence gifts on behalf of the court, and the Türks then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsun, commander of Feng prefecture, sent Gao Jing beyond the border with the tribute as condolence gifts from the court, and the Türks withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚午，梁師都寇靈州，長史楊則擊走之。

translations.literal: Third month, day Gengwu: Liang Shidu raided Ling prefecture and was driven off by the chief administrator Yang Ze.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Gengwu, Liang Shidu raided Ling prefecture and was repulsed by chief administrator Yang Ze.

sentences.zh: 壬申，王世充寇穀州，刺史史萬寶戰不利。

translations.literal: On day Renshen, Wang Shichong raided Gu prefecture; the governor Shi Wanbao fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshen, Wang Shichong attacked Gu prefecture, and governor Shi Wanbao was defeated.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，隋北海通守鄭虔符、文登令方惠整及東海、齊郡、東平、任城、平陸、壽張、須昌賊帥王薄等並以其地來降。

translations.literal: On day Gengchen, Zheng Qianfu, Sui communications commissioner of Beihai, Fang Huizheng, magistrate of Wendeng, and the bandit chiefs Wang Bo and others of Donghai, Qi commandery, Dongping, Rencheng, Pinglu, Shouzhang, and Xuchang all surrendered their territories.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengchen, Zheng Qianfu, Sui communications commissioner of Beihai, Fang Huizheng, magistrate of Wendeng, and the bandit leader Wang Bo and others from Donghai, Qi, Dongping, Rencheng, Pinglu, Shouzhang, and Xuchang all submitted their territories.

sentences.zh: 王世充之寇新安也。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong raided Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong attacked Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 外示攻取，實召文武之附己者議受禪。

translations.literal: Outwardly he showed an attack, but in fact he summoned civil and military officials loyal to him to discuss accepting the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was making war, but in fact he summoned loyal officials to discuss taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 李世英深以為不可，曰：「四方所以奔馳歸附東都者，以公能中興隋室故也。

translations.literal: Li Shiying deeply held this impossible and said: 'The reason the four quarters have rushed to attach themselves to the Eastern Capital is that you can revive the house of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiying strongly opposed the idea, saying: 'The four quarters have rallied to the Eastern Capital because they believe you can restore the Sui.

sentences.zh: 今九州之地，未清其一，遽正位號，恐遠人皆思叛去矣！」

translations.literal: Now of the nine provinces' lands not one is yet pacified. If you hastily assume the imperial title, I fear distant peoples will all think of rebelling and leaving!'
translations.idiomatic: Not one of the nine provinces is yet pacified. If you declare yourself emperor now, I fear the distant regions will turn away!'

sentences.zh: 世充曰：「公言是也！」

translations.literal: Shichong said: 'Your words are right!'
translations.idiomatic: Shichong said: 'You are right!'

sentences.zh: 長史韋節、楊續等曰：「隋氏數窮，在理昭然。

translations.literal: The chief administrators Wei Jie, Yang Xu, and others said: 'The Sui house's fate is exhausted—this is clear in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrators Wei Jie, Yang Xu, and others said: 'The Sui mandate is clearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 夫非常之事，固不可與常人議之。」

translations.literal: Such an extraordinary matter cannot be discussed with ordinary men.'
translations.idiomatic: An extraordinary matter such as this cannot be debated with ordinary men.'

sentences.zh: 太史令樂德融曰：「昔歲長星出，乃除舊布新之征；

translations.literal: The Director of Astronomy Yue Derong said: 'Last year a long comet appeared—a sign of removing the old and establishing the new.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Astronomy Yue Derong said: 'Last year a long comet appeared, a sign of removing the old and establishing the new.

sentences.zh: 今歲星在角、亢。

translations.literal: This year the Year Star is in Jiao and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: This year the Year Star stands in Jiao and Kang.

sentences.zh: 亢，鄭之分野。

translations.literal: Kang is the territorial division of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kang is the astral domain of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 若不亟順天道，恐王氣衰息。」

translations.literal: If you do not quickly follow Heaven's way, I fear the royal aura will wane.'
translations.idiomatic: If you do not quickly follow Heaven's mandate, I fear your royal fortune will fade.'

sentences.zh: 世充從之。

translations.literal: Shichong followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong accepted this counsel.

sentences.zh: 外兵曹參軍戴冑言於世充曰：「君臣猶父子也，休戚同之，明公莫若竭忠徇國，則家國俱安矣。」

translations.literal: Dai Zhou, an official of the Outer Bureau of Military Affairs, said to Shichong: 'Ruler and minister are like father and son, sharing fortune and misfortune alike. Your Excellency would do better to exhaust loyalty and die for the state—then family and realm will both be secure.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou of the Outer Bureau of Military Affairs told Shichong: 'Ruler and minister are like father and son and share the same fate. Your Excellency would do better to serve the state with full loyalty—then both your house and the realm will be secure.'

sentences.zh: 世充詭辭稱善而遣之，世充議受九錫，冑復固諫，世充怒，出為鄭州長史，使與兄子行本鎮虎牢。

translations.literal: Shichong answered with deceptive words praising him and sent him away. When Shichong discussed receiving the Nine Bestowals, Zhou again remonstrated firmly. Shichong was angry and sent him out as chief administrator of Zheng prefecture, having him and his elder brother's son Xingben garrison Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong answered politely and dismissed him. When Shichong discussed receiving the Nine Bestowals, Zhou remonstrated again. Shichong was furious and sent him out as chief administrator of Zheng prefecture, posting him with his nephew Xingben to garrison Hulao.

sentences.zh: 乃使段達等言於皇泰主，請加世充九錫。

translations.literal: He then had Duan Da and others speak to Emperor Gong, requesting that the Nine Bestowals be granted to Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Duan Da and others ask Emperor Gong to grant Shichong the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主曰：「鄭公近平李密，已拜太尉，自是以來，未有殊績，俟天下稍平，議之未晚。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gong said: 'Prince Zheng recently pacified Li Mi and was already appointed Grand Marshal. Since then he has had no special achievements. Wait until the realm is somewhat settled—it is not too late to discuss this.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong said: 'Prince Zheng has only recently defeated Li Mi and was made Grand Marshal. Since then he has done nothing especially meritorious. Wait until the realm is somewhat settled—it will not be too late.'

sentences.zh: 段達曰：「太尉欲之。」

translations.literal: Duan Da said: 'The Grand Marshal wants them.'
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da said: 'The Grand Marshal wants them.'

sentences.zh: 皇泰主熟視達曰：「任公！」

translations.literal: Emperor Gong stared fixedly at Da and said: 'Lord Ren!'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong stared hard at Da and said: 'Lord Ren!'

sentences.zh: 辛巳，達等以皇泰主之詔，命世充為相國，假黃鉞，總百揆，進爵鄭王，加九錫，鄭國置丞相以下官。

translations.literal: On day Xinsi, Da and others, by Emperor Gong's edict, appointed Shichong Chancellor of State, granted him the yellow battle-axe, put all government affairs under his control, advanced him to Prince of Zheng, added the Nine Bestowals, and established for the state of Zheng offices from Chancellor downward.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinsi, by Emperor Gong's edict conveyed through Da and the others, Shichong was made Chancellor of State with the yellow battle-axe, given control of all government affairs, enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng with the Nine Bestowals, and granted a full state apparatus for Zheng.

sentences.zh: 初，宇文化及以隋大理卿鄭善果為民部尚書。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuwen Huaji had appointed the Sui Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Shanguo Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuwen Huaji had appointed Zheng Shanguo, Sui Director of the Court of Judicial Review, as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 從至聊城，為化及督戰，中流矢。

translations.literal: He followed to Liaocheng and directed battle for Huaji, taking an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Huaji to Liaocheng and directed the fighting there, where he was struck by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 竇建德克聊城，王琮獲善果，責之曰：「公名臣之家，隋室大臣，奈何為弒君之賊效命，苦戰傷痍至此乎！」

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande took Liaocheng, Wang Cong captured Shanguo and reproached him: 'Your house is one of eminent ministers, a great minister of the Sui house—how could you serve the regicide traitor and fight bitterly until wounded to this point!'
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande captured Liaocheng, Wang Cong seized Shanguo and rebuked him: 'You come from a house of eminent ministers and served the Sui as a great official—how could you fight so desperately for a regicide that you are wounded like this!'

sentences.zh: 善果大慚，欲自殺，宋正本馳往救止之；

translations.literal: Shanguo was deeply ashamed and wished to kill himself. Song Zhengben galloped to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was deeply ashamed and tried to kill himself, but Song Zhengben rushed to stop him.

sentences.zh: 建德復不為禮，乃奔相州，淮安王神通送之長安。

translations.literal: Jiande again showed him no courtesy, so he fled to Xiang prefecture, and Prince Huai'an Shentong sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande treated him coldly, so he fled to Xiang prefecture, and Prince Huai'an Shentong sent him on to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 庚午，善果至，上優禮之，拜左庶子、檢校內史待郎。

translations.literal: On day Gengwu, Shanguo arrived. The emperor treated him with exceptional courtesy and appointed him Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengwu, Shanguo arrived. The emperor received him with exceptional honor and appointed him Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉諷并州父老詣闕留己；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi Yuanji prompted the elders of Bing prefecture to go to court and ask that he be kept there.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Yuanji prompted the elders of Bing prefecture to petition the court to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 甲申，復以元吉為并州總管。

translations.literal: On day Jiashen, Yuanji was again appointed commander of Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiashen, Yuanji was reappointed commander of Bing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊子，淮南五州皆遣使來降。

translations.literal: On day Wuzi, all five prefectures of Huainan sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuzi, all five Huainan prefectures sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，劉武周寇并州。

translations.literal: On day Xinmao, Liu Wuzhou raided Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao, Liu Wuzhou attacked Bing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，營州總管鄧暠擊高開道，敗之。

translations.literal: On day Renchen, Deng Gao, commander of Ying prefecture, attacked Gao Kaidao and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renchen, Deng Gao, commander of Ying prefecture, attacked Gao Kaidao and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 甲午，王世充遣其將高毘寇義州。

translations.literal: On day Jiawu, Wang Shichong sent his general Gao Pi to raid Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiawu, Wang Shichong sent his general Gao Pi to attack Yi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東都道士桓法嗣獻《孔子閉房記》於王世充，言「相國當代隋為天子」。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital Daoist Huan Fasi presented the Record of Confucius in Seclusion to Wang Shichong, saying 'The Chancellor of State should replace the Sui as Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Huan Fasi of the Eastern Capital presented the Record of Confucius in Seclusion to Wang Shichong, declaring that 'the Chancellor of State is destined to replace the Sui as emperor.'

sentences.zh: 世充大悅，以法嗣為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly pleased and made Fasi a Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was delighted and made Fasi a Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 世充又羅取雜鳥，書帛繫頸，自言符命而縱之。

translations.literal: Shichong also caught miscellaneous birds, wrote on silk and tied it to their necks proclaiming his mandate, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong also caught birds, tied silk messages proclaiming his heavenly mandate around their necks, and released them.

sentences.zh: 有得鳥來獻者，亦拜官爵。

translations.literal: Those who obtained such birds and presented them were also granted offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who caught such a bird and presented it was also rewarded with office and rank.

sentences.zh: 於是段達以皇泰主命，加世充殊禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duan Da, by Emperor Gong's command, granted Shichong extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Then, by Emperor Gong's command conveyed through Duan Da, Shichong was granted extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 世充奉表三讓，百官勸進，設位於都常。

translations.literal: Shichong submitted memorials declining three times; the hundred officials urged his advance; the seat was set up at the capital's regular place.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong submitted three formal refusals; the officials urged him to accept; the throne was set up at the usual place in the capital.

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威年老，不任朝謁，世充以威隋氏重臣，欲以炫耀士民，每勸進，必冠威名。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat Su Wei was old and could not attend court audiences. Shichong, because Wei was a weighty minister of the Sui house and wished to dazzle scholars and commoners, at every urging of advance always placed Wei's name at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Director of the Secretariat, was too old for court audiences. Shichong, wishing to impress the people by displaying a great Sui minister, always listed Wei's name first among those urging his accession.

sentences.zh: 及受殊禮之日，扶威置百官之上，然後南面正坐受之。

translations.literal: On the day he received the extraordinary honors, he supported Wei and placed him above the hundred officials, then sat facing south in the correct seat to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received the extraordinary honors, he had Wei supported to a place above all the officials, then took the throne facing south.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，劉武周引突厥之眾，軍於黃蛇嶺，兵鋒甚盛。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Liu Wuzhou led Türk forces and encamped at Huangshe Ridge; his military momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, Liu Wuzhou led Türk forces to Huangshe Ridge, and his army's momentum was formidable.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉使車騎將軍張達以步卒百人嘗寇；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi Yuanji sent the Chariots and Cavalry general Zhang Da with a hundred infantry to probe the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Yuanji sent Chariots and Cavalry general Zhang Da with a hundred infantry to probe the enemy.

sentences.zh: 達辭以兵少不可往，元吉強遣之，至則俱沒。

translations.literal: Da declined on the grounds that his troops were too few to go; Yuanji forced him to go, and when he arrived they were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Da protested that his force was too small, but Yuanji insisted. When they arrived, the entire detachment was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 達忿恨，庚子，引武周襲榆次，陷之。

translations.literal: Da nursed resentment; on the day Gengzi he led Liu Wuzhou to raid Yuci and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, Zhang Da, on the day Gengzi, brought Liu Wuzhou to strike at Yuci and took the city.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍段確，性嗜酒，奉詔慰勞朱粲於菊潭。

translations.literal: Duan Que, Irregular Attendant-in-Ordinary, was by nature fond of wine; by imperial edict he went to comfort and reward Zhu Can at Jutan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Que, an Irregular Attendant-in-Ordinary, was a heavy drinker. By imperial order he went to Jutan to console and reward Zhu Can.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，乘醉侮粲曰：「聞卿好□敢人，人作何味？」

translations.literal: On the day Xinchou, riding his drunkenness he insulted Can, saying, "I hear you like to devour people—what do people taste like?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinchou, drunk, he mocked Zhu Can: "They say you like to devour human flesh. What do people taste like?"

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「□敢醉人正如糟藏彘肉。」

translations.literal: Can said, "Devouring drunk men is just like pork pickled in lees."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can replied, "Eating a drunk man is no different from pork cured in wine lees."

sentences.zh: 確怒，罵曰：「狂賊入朝，為一頭奴耳，復得□敢人乎！」

translations.literal: Que grew angry and cursed, "Mad bandit in court—you are nothing but a slave's head. Can you devour people again!"
translations.idiomatic: Que flew into a rage and cursed him: "You mad rebel dare enter court—you are nothing but a slave's head. Do you think you can devour people again!"

sentences.zh: 粲於座收確及從者數十人，悉烹之，以□敢左右。

translations.literal: At the feast Can seized Que and several dozen attendants, boiled them all, and had those beside him devour them.
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet Zhu Can seized Que and several dozen of his attendants, had them all boiled, and made those beside him eat the flesh.

sentences.zh: 遂屠菊潭，奔王世充，世充以為龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: He then massacred Jutan, fled to Wang Shichong, and Shichong appointed him Grand General of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Jutan to the sword, fled to Wang Shichong, and Shichong made him Grand General of the Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 王世充令長史韋節、楊續等及太常博士衡水孔穎達，造禪代儀，遣段達、雲定興等十餘人入奏皇泰主曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下遵唐、虞之跡。」

translations.literal: Wang Shichong ordered Chief Secretaries Wei Jie and Yang Xu and others, together with Erudite of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices Kong Yingda of Hengshui, to devise the ritual for abdication and succession; he sent Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and more than ten others to memorialize to Emperor Yang Tong, saying, "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great. We hope Your Majesty will follow the example of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong ordered his chief secretaries Wei Jie and Yang Xu, together with Erudite of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices Kong Yingda of Hengshui, to draw up the rites of abdication and succession. He sent Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and more than a dozen others to present a memorial to Emperor Yang Tong: "Heaven's mandate shifts; the Prince of Zheng's merit is overwhelming. We beg Your Majesty to follow the path of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 皇泰主斂膝據案，怒曰：「天下，高祖之天下，若隋祚未亡，此言不應輒發；

translations.literal: Emperor Yang Tong drew up his knees and leaned on the desk, saying angrily, "The realm is the realm of the Founding Emperor. If the fortune of Sui has not yet perished, such words ought not to be uttered lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang Tong drew up his knees against the desk and said in anger, "This realm belongs to the Founding Emperor of Sui. If the house of Sui is not yet ended, such words should never have been spoken.

sentences.zh: 必天命已改，何煩禪讓！

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate has indeed changed, why trouble with abdication!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's mandate has already turned elsewhere, why bother with a ceremonial transfer of the throne!

sentences.zh: 公等或祖檷舊臣，或台鼎高位，既有斯言，朕復何望！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen are either old ministers who served my ancestors or holders of the highest offices at the imperial altar—now that such words have been spoken, what hope have I left!"
translations.idiomatic: You are either ministers who served my forebears or men who hold the highest offices in the land. Now that you have spoken thus, what is left for me to hope for!"

sentences.zh: 顏色凜冽，在廷者皆流汗。

translations.literal: His expression was severe and cold; all those in court broke into sweat.
translations.idiomatic: His face was ice. Everyone present broke into a cold sweat.

sentences.zh: 退朝，泣對太后。

translations.literal: After court he withdrew and wept before the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When court adjourned, he withdrew and wept before the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 世充更使人謂之曰：「今海內未寧，須立長君，俟四方安集，當復子明辟，必如前誓。」

translations.literal: Shichong again sent someone to tell him, "The realm within the seas is not yet at peace; a mature ruler must be installed. When the four quarters are settled and gathered, the son will be restored to the illuminated throne—this is sure, as in the former oath."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent another messenger to tell him, "The realm is still unsettled. We need a seasoned ruler for now. When the four quarters are pacified, your son will be restored to the throne—just as we swore before."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，世充稱皇泰主命，禪位於鄭。

translations.literal: On the day Guimao, Shichong, claiming it was by Emperor Yang Tong's command, had the throne abdicated to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guimao, Shichong, claiming to act on Emperor Yang Tong's order, had the throne transferred to the house of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 遣其兄世惲幽皇泰主於含涼殿，雖有三表陳讓及敕書敦勸，皇泰主皆不知也。

translations.literal: He sent his elder brother Shi Yun to confine Emperor Yang Tong in Hanliang Hall. Although there were three memorials of declining and edicts earnestly urging acceptance, Emperor Yang Tong knew nothing of them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his elder brother Shi Yun to confine Emperor Yang Tong in Hanliang Hall. Though three memorials of refusal and imperial edicts pressing him to accept were issued, the emperor knew nothing of any of it.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將引兵入清宮城，又遣術人以桃湯葦火祓除禁省。

translations.literal: He sent generals to lead troops into the palace to clear it, and also sent ritual specialists to purify the forbidden precinct with peach broth and reed fire.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals to march troops through the palace to clear it, and ritual specialists to purify the inner court with peach broth and reed-flame rites.

sentences.zh: 隋將帥、郡縣及賊帥前後繼有降者，詔以王薄為齊州總管，伏德為濟州總管，鄭虔符為青州總管，綦公順為淮州總管，王孝師為滄州總管。

translations.literal: Sui generals, prefectures and counties, and bandit chiefs surrendered one after another; an edict appointed Wang Bo regional commander of Qi Prefecture, Fu De of Ji, Zheng Qianfu of Qing, Qi Gongshun of Huai, and Wang Xiaoshi of Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui commanders, prefectural officials, and rebel leaders kept surrendering in succession. An edict appointed Wang Bo regional commander of Qi, Fu De of Ji, Zheng Qianfu of Qing, Qi Gongshun of Huai, and Wang Xiaoshi of Cang.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣大理卿新樂郎楚之安撫山東，秘書監夏侯端安撫淮左。

translations.literal: On the day Jiachen, the Director of the Court of Judicial Review Lang Chuzhi of Xinle was sent to pacify Shandong, and the Director of the Secretariat Xiahou Duan to pacify the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiachen, Lang Chuzhi of Xinle, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was dispatched to pacify Shandong, and Xiahou Duan, Director of the Secretariat, to pacify the lands along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，王世充備法駕入宮，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day Yisi, Wang Shichong, with the full imperial equipage, entered the palace and ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yisi, Wang Shichong entered the palace with the full imperial retinue and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大赦，改元開明。

translations.literal: On the day Bingwu he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Kaiming.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingwu he declared a general amnesty and proclaimed the era name Kaiming.

sentences.zh: 丁未，隋御衛將軍陳稜以江都來降；

translations.literal: On the day Dingwei, the Sui Imperial Guard general Chen Ling came to surrender with Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingwei, the Sui Imperial Guard general Chen Ling surrendered, bringing Jiangdu with him.

sentences.zh: 以稜為揚州總管。

translations.literal: Ling was appointed regional commander of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling was appointed regional commander of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊申，王世充立子玄應為太子，玄恕為漢王，余兄弟宗族十九人皆為王。

translations.literal: On the day Wushen, Wang Shichong installed his son Xuanying as heir apparent and Xuanxu as Prince of Han; the remaining brothers and clansmen, nineteen in all, were all made princes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wushen, Wang Shichong named his son Xuanying crown prince and Xuanxu Prince of Han. Nineteen other brothers and kinsmen were all ennobled as princes.

sentences.zh: 奉皇泰主為潞國公。
