translations.literal: Emperor Yang Tong was honored as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang Tong was given the title Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 以蘇威為太師，段達為司徒，雲定興為太尉，張僅為司空，楊續為納言，韋節為內史，王隆為左僕射，韋霽為右僕射，齊王世惲為尚書令，楊汪為吏部尚書，杜淹為少吏部，鄭頲為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Su Wei was made Grand Preceptor, Duan Da Minister over the Masses, Yun Dingxing Grand Marshal, Zhang Jin Minister of Works, Yang Xu Director of the Palace Secretariat, Wei Jie Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Wang Long Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wei Ji Right Vice Director, Prince of Qi Shi Yun Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Yang Wang Minister of Personnel, Du Yan Vice Minister of Personnel, and Zheng Ting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei was appointed Grand Preceptor; Duan Da, Minister over the Masses; Yun Dingxing, Grand Marshal; Zhang Jin, Minister of Works; Yang Xu, Director of the Palace Secretariat; Wei Jie, Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Wang Long, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Wei Ji, Right Vice Director; Prince of Qi Shi Yun, Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Yang Wang, Minister of Personnel; Du Yan, Vice Minister of Personnel; and Zheng Ting, Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 世惲，世充之兄也。

translations.literal: Shi Yun was Shichong's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yun was Wang Shichong's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 又以國子助都吳人陸德明為漢王師，令玄恕就其家行束脩禮。

translations.literal: He also appointed Lu Deming of Wu, an assistant at the Imperial University in the capital, tutor to the Prince of Han, and ordered Xuanxu to go to his home to perform the ceremony of presenting the bundle of dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Lu Deming of Wu, an assistant at the Imperial University, tutor to the Prince of Han, and ordered Xuanxu to visit his home and perform the ceremony of presenting the bundle of dried meat as a pupil's gift.

sentences.zh: 德明恥之，故服巴豆散，臥稱病，玄恕入跪床下，對之遺利，竟不與語。

translations.literal: Deming was shamed by this; he therefore took croton powder, lay abed claiming illness, and when Xuanxu entered and knelt beneath the bed, relieved himself in his presence—yet he would not speak with him at all.
translations.idiomatic: Deming was mortified. He took a dose of croton powder, lay in bed feigning illness, and when Xuanxu came in and knelt beneath the bed, voided his bowels in the prince's presence—yet never spoke a word to him.

sentences.zh: 德明名朗，以字行。

translations.literal: Deming's given name was Lang; he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Deming's given name was Lang; he was known by his style name rather than his personal name.

sentences.zh: 世充於闕下及玄武門等數處皆設榻，坐無常所，親受章表。

translations.literal: Shichong set up couches below the palace gate and at several places such as the Xuanwu Gate; he had no fixed seat and personally received memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong set up couches below the palace gate and at several places including the Xuanwu Gate. He had no fixed seat and personally received petitions and memorials.

sentences.zh: 或輕騎遊歷衢市，亦不清道，民但避路而已。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode lightly through the streets and markets; the road was not cleared, and the people merely stepped aside.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he rode lightly through the streets and markets without having the road cleared; the people simply stepped out of his way.

sentences.zh: 世充按轡徐行，語之曰：「昔時天子深居九重，在下事情無由聞徹。

translations.literal: Shichong held the reins and moved slowly, saying to them, "In former times the Son of Heaven dwelt deep within the ninefold palace; affairs below had no way of being heard in full.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong held his reins and moved slowly along, telling the crowd, "In the old days the Son of Heaven dwelt deep within the ninefold palace, and what happened below never reached his ears.

sentences.zh: 今世充非貪天位，但欲救恤時危，正如一州刺史，親覽庶務，當與士庶共評朝政，尚恐門有禁限，今於門外設坐聽朝，宜各盡情。」

translations.literal: Now Shichong does not covet Heaven's throne; he only wishes to relieve the crisis of the age, just like a prefect of a single province personally reviewing common affairs. I ought to judge court policy together with scholars and commoners. I still fear that gates impose restrictions; now I have set a seat outside the gate to hear court—each of you should speak your mind fully."
translations.idiomatic: I do not covet the throne. I only wish to rescue the realm from crisis, like a provincial governor who personally oversees every affair. I mean to discuss state policy with scholars and commoners alike. I still fear that palace gates shut people out—so I have set a seat outside the gate to hold court. Speak freely."

sentences.zh: 又令西朝堂納冤抑，東朝堂納直諫。

translations.literal: He also ordered the western audience hall to receive those suffering wrongful oppression and the eastern audience hall to receive forthright remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the western audience hall to receive petitions about wrongful oppression and the eastern hall to receive frank remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 於是獻策上書者日有數百，條疏既煩，省覽難遍，數日後，不復更出。

translations.literal: Thereupon those presenting stratagems and memorials numbered several hundred a day; the items and summaries were already burdensome, and review could not cover them all. After several days he no longer appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Within days hundreds of people were submitting plans and memorials each day. The flood of documents was overwhelming, and he could not read them all. After a few days he stopped appearing altogether.

sentences.zh: 竇建德聞王世充自立，乃絕之，始建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，下書稱詔，追謚隋煬帝為閔帝。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande heard that Wang Shichong had declared himself emperor and thereupon broke with him; he first raised the Son of Heaven's banners, went out and in with imperial escort, issued documents styled as edicts, and posthumously honored Emperor Yang of Sui with the temple name Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande learned that Wang Shichong had declared himself emperor, he broke with him, raised the imperial banners, traveled with full royal escort, issued documents in the style of imperial edicts, and posthumously honored Emperor Yang of Sui with the temple name Min.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕之死也，有遣腹子政道，建德立以為鄖公，然猶依倚突厥，以壯其兵勢。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Yang Jian died, he left a posthumous son Zhengdao; Jiande installed him as Duke of Yun, yet still relied on the Turks to strengthen his military power.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Yang Jian died, he left a posthumous son, Zhengdao. Jiande installed him as Duke of Yun, yet still leaned on the Turks to bolster his armies.

sentences.zh: 隋義成公主遣使迎蕭皇后及南陽公主，建德遣千餘騎送之，又傳宇文化及首以獻義成公主。

translations.literal: The Sui Princess Yicheng sent envoys to welcome Empress Xiao and the Princess of Nanyang; Jiande dispatched more than a thousand horsemen to escort them, and also forwarded the head of Yuwen Huaji as an offering to Princess Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Princess Yicheng sent envoys to escort Empress Xiao and the Princess of Nanyang home. Jiande dispatched more than a thousand horsemen to see them on their way and also sent Yuwen Huaji's head as a gift to Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，劉武周圍并州，齊王元吉拒卻之。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen, Liu Wuzhou besieged Bing Prefecture; Prince of Qi Yuanji repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen, Liu Wuzhou besieged Bing Prefecture, and Prince Qi Yuanji drove him back.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔太常卿李仲文將兵救并州。

translations.literal: On the day Wuwu an edict ordered the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Li Zhongwen to lead troops to relieve Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuwu an edict ordered Li Zhongwen, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, to march to the relief of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王世充將軍丘懷義居門下內省。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Qiu Huaiyi lodged in the Gate Department's inner office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's general Qiu Huaiyi was quartered in the inner offices of the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 召越王君度、漢王玄恕、將軍郭士衡雜妓妾飲博，侍御史張蘊古彈之。

translations.literal: He summoned Prince of Yue Jun Du, Prince of Han Xuanxu, and General Guo Shiheng to drink and gamble with assorted singing girls and concubines; the Attending Censor Zhang Yungu impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Prince of Yue Jun Du, Prince of Han Xuanxu, and General Guo Shiheng to drink and gamble with singing girls and concubines. Attending Censor Zhang Yungu impeached them.

sentences.zh: 世充大怒，令散手執君度、玄恕，批其耳數十；

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly angered and ordered guards to seize Jun Du and Xuanxu and slap their ears several dozen times.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong flew into a rage and ordered his guards to seize Jun Du and Xuanxu and slap their ears several dozen times.

sentences.zh: 又命引入東上閣，仗之各數十。

translations.literal: He also ordered them brought into the eastern upper pavilion and beaten with staves, each several dozen blows.
translations.idiomatic: He then had them brought into the eastern upper pavilion and beaten with staves, each receiving several dozen blows.

sentences.zh: 懷義、士衡不問。

translations.literal: Huaiyi and Shiheng were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi and Shiheng went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 賞蘊古帛百段，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yungu was rewarded with a hundred bolts of silk and promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yungu was rewarded with a hundred bolts of silk and promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 君度，世充之兄子也。

translations.literal: Jun Du was Shichong's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Du was the son of Wang Shichong's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 世充每聽朝，殷勤誨諭，言詞重複，千端萬緒，侍衛之人不勝倦弊，百司奏事，疲於聽受。

translations.literal: Whenever Shichong held court he earnestly instructed and admonished, his words repetitive, his topics by the thousands and tens of thousands; the guards could not bear the weariness, and the hundred offices reporting affairs were exhausted from listening.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shichong held court he lectured at length, repeating himself endlessly on a thousand matters at once. His guards were worn to exhaustion, and the officials presenting business were numb from listening.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫蘇良諫曰：「陛下語太多而無領要，計云爾即可，何煩許辭也！」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Su Liang remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty's words are too many and without a leading thread. If the plan is thus, that is enough—why trouble with so many phrases!"
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Su Liang remonstrated: "Your Majesty speaks too much and never gets to the point. If the plan is settled, that is enough—why waste so many words!"

sentences.zh: 世充默然良久，亦不罪良，然性如是，終不能改也。

translations.literal: Shichong was silent a long while and did not punish Liang either, yet his nature being such, in the end he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong fell silent for a long while and did not punish Liang—but that was his nature, and he never changed.

sentences.zh: 王世充數攻伊州，總管張善相拒之；

translations.literal: Wang Shichong repeatedly attacked Yi Prefecture; the regional commander Zhang Shanxiang resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong attacked Yi Prefecture again and again; regional commander Zhang Shanxiang held him off.

sentences.zh: 糧盡，援兵不至，癸亥，城陷，善相罵世充極口而死。

translations.literal: Provisions were exhausted and relief troops did not arrive; on the day Guihai the city fell, and Shanxiang cursed Shichong to the utmost with his mouth and died.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out and no relief came, the city fell on the day Guihai. Shanxiang cursed Shichong with his last breath and died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，歎曰：「吾負善相，善相不負吾也！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he sighed and said, "I failed Shanxiang; Shanxiang did not fail me!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard the news, he sighed and said, "I failed Shanxiang—but Shanxiang did not fail me."

sentences.zh: 賜其子爵襄城郡公。

translations.literal: He bestowed on his son the title Marquis of Xiangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Shanxiang's son as Marquis of Xiangcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五月，王世充陷義州，復寇西濟州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wang Shichong captured Yi Prefecture and again raided western Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Wang Shichong took Yi Prefecture and again raided western Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣右驍衛大將軍劉弘基將兵救之。

translations.literal: He sent the Right General of the Valiant Cavalry Liu Hongji to lead troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Hongji, Right General of the Valiant Cavalry, to march to its relief.

sentences.zh: 李軌將安修仁兄興貴，仕長安，表請說軌，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Li Gui's general An Xinggui, elder brother of An Xiuren, served at Chang'an and submitted a memorial asking to go persuade Li Gui, instructing him on fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui, elder brother of Li Gui's general An Xiuren, was serving at Chang'an. He submitted a memorial asking permission to go persuade Li Gui, setting out the consequences of fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「軌阻兵恃險，連結吐谷渾、突厥，吾興兵擊之，尚恐不克，豈口舌所能下乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Li Gui blocks the army and relies on perilous terrain, linking with the Tuyuhun and the Turks. If I raise troops to strike him, I still fear I may not overcome him—how could words and mouth bring him down!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Li Gui holds the passes and leans on rugged terrain, with the Tuyuhun and the Turks at his side. I am not sure I could defeat him even with an army—how could mere words bring him down!"

sentences.zh: 興貴曰：「臣家在涼州，奕世豪望，為民夷所附；

translations.literal: Xinggui said, "Your servant's family is in Liang Prefecture, with hereditary magnate prestige, and is attached to by both Chinese and barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui said, "My family has been in Liangzhou for generations, with great prestige among both Chinese and non-Chinese peoples.

sentences.zh: 弟修仁為軌所信任，子弟在機近者以十數。

translations.literal: My younger brother Xiuren is trusted by Li Gui, and kinsmen in positions close to power number more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Xiuren enjoys Li Gui's trust, and more than a dozen of our kinsmen hold posts near the center of power.

sentences.zh: 臣往說之，軌聽臣固善，若其不聽，圖之肘腋，易矣！」

translations.literal: If your servant goes to persuade him and Li Gui listens, that is naturally good; if he does not listen, to plot against him from within his armpit is easy!"
translations.idiomatic: If I go to persuade him and he listens, all the better. If he refuses, striking from within his own circle will be easy."

sentences.zh: 上乃遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon sent him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 興貴至武威，軌以為左右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Xinggui arrived at Wuwei; Li Gui appointed him Grand General of the Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinggui reached Wuwei, Li Gui appointed him Grand General of the Left and Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 興貴乘間說軌曰：「涼地不過千里，土薄民貧。

translations.literal: Xinggui seized an opportunity to say to Li Gui, "The Liang region is no more than a thousand li; the soil is thin and the people poor.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing a private moment, Xinggui said to Li Gui, "The Liang region spans barely a thousand li. The land is poor and the people are few.

sentences.zh: 今唐起太原，取函秦，宰制中原。

translations.literal: Now Tang has risen at Taiyuan, taken Hangu and Qin, and holds sway over the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Tang has risen at Taiyuan, taken the Hangu and Qin regions, and now dominates the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 戰必勝，攻必取，此殆天啟，非人力也。

translations.literal: In battle they are sure to win, in attack sure to take—this is nearly Heaven's opening, not human effort.
translations.idiomatic: They win every battle and take every city they besiege. This is Heaven's mandate, not mere human strength.

sentences.zh: 不若舉河西歸之，則竇融之功復見於今日矣！」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to offer the Hexi region in submission? Then Dou Rong's achievement would appear again in our day!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to submit the Hexi region to Tang and win for yourself the glory that Dou Rong won in his day!"

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「吾據山河之固，彼雖強大，若我何？

translations.literal: Li Gui said, "I hold the solidity of mountains and rivers; however strong they are, what can they do to me?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said, "I hold the natural defenses of mountains and rivers. However strong they are, what can they do to me?

sentences.zh: 汝自唐來，為唐遊說耳。」

translations.literal: You came from Tang—you are lobbying for Tang, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: You came from Tang. You are nothing but Tang's mouthpiece."

sentences.zh: 興貴謝曰：「臣聞富貴不歸故鄉，如衣繡夜行。

translations.literal: Xinggui apologized, saying, "Your servant has heard that wealth and honor not returned to one's homeland are like wearing brocade and walking at night.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui apologized: "I have heard that wealth and honor mean nothing if you cannot show them in your homeland—as pointless as wearing brocade in the dark.

sentences.zh: 臣闔門受陛下榮祿，安肯附唐！

translations.literal: Your servant's entire household has received Your Majesty's honors and stipends—how could I be willing to attach myself to Tang!
translations.idiomatic: My whole family lives on Your Majesty's bounty. Why would I ever side with Tang!

sentences.zh: 但欲效其愚慮，可否在陛下耳。」

translations.literal: I only wish to offer my foolish counsel; whether it is acceptable rests with Your Majesty alone."
translations.idiomatic: I only wished to offer my honest counsel. Whether you accept it is entirely for Your Majesty to decide."

sentences.zh: 於是退與修仁陰結諸胡起兵擊軌，軌出戰而敗，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew and secretly joined with Xiuren to rally the various Hu in revolt against Li Gui; Li Gui went out to battle and was defeated, then sealed the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and secretly joined Xiuren in rallying the non-Chinese peoples to rise against Li Gui. Li Gui marched out, was defeated, and sealed himself inside the city.

sentences.zh: 興貴徇曰：「大唐遣我來誅李軌，敢助之者夷三族！」

translations.literal: Xinggui proclaimed through the army, "Great Tang sent me to execute Li Gui—whoever dares aid him, three generations shall be exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui proclaimed through the city: "Great Tang sent me to execute Li Gui. Whoever dares help him will see three generations of his family wiped out!"

sentences.zh: 城中人爭出就興貴。

translations.literal: The people in the city vied to go out to Xinggui.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the city rushed out to join Xinggui.

sentences.zh: 軌計窮，與妻子登玉女台，置酒為別。

translations.literal: Li Gui's stratagems exhausted, he ascended the Jade Maiden Tower with his wife and children and set out wine for a farewell.
translations.idiomatic: With no options left, Li Gui climbed the Jade Maiden Tower with his wife and children and poured a farewell cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，興貴執之以聞，河西悉平。

translations.literal: On the day Gengchen, Xinggui seized him and reported it; the Hexi region was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengchen, Xinggui seized him and reported the capture. The entire Hexi region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 鄧曉在長安，舞蹈稱慶，上曰：「汝為人使臣，聞國亡，不戚而喜，以求媚於朕。

translations.literal: Deng Xiao was at Chang'an; he danced and proclaimed congratulations. The Emperor said, "You served another as envoy; hearing that state perish, you were not sorrowful but glad, seeking to flatter me.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xiao was in Chang'an. He danced and proclaimed his congratulations. The Emperor said, "You were another man's envoy. When you heard his state had fallen, you were not grieved but glad—seeking only to flatter me.

sentences.zh: 不忠於李軌，肯為朕用乎！」

translations.literal: Disloyal to Li Gui—would you be willing to serve me!"
translations.idiomatic: If you were disloyal to Li Gui, why would I ever trust you!"

sentences.zh: 遂廢之終身。

translations.literal: He thereupon dismissed him for life.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed him from office for life.

sentences.zh: 軌至長安，並其子弟皆伏誅。

translations.literal: When Li Gui reached Chang'an, he and his sons and younger brothers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gui reached Chang'an, he and all his sons and brothers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 以安興貴為右武候大將軍、上柱國、涼國公，賜帛萬段，安修仁為左武候大將軍、申國公。

translations.literal: An Xinggui was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Liang, and bestowed ten thousand bolts of silk; An Xiuren was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Liang, with ten thousand bolts of silk as reward. An Xiuren was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 隋末，離石胡劉龍兒擁兵數萬，自號劉王，以其子季真為太子；

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, the Lishi Hu Liu Long'er gathered several tens of thousands of troops, styled himself King Liu, and made his son Jizhen crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui, the Lishi Hu chieftain Liu Long'er raised an army of tens of thousands, declared himself King Liu, and named his son Jizhen crown prince.

sentences.zh: 虎賁郎將梁德擊斬龍兒。

translations.literal: The Tiger Guard commandant Liang De attacked and beheaded Long'er.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard commandant Liang De attacked and killed Long'er.

sentences.zh: 至是，季真與弟六兒復舉兵為亂，引劉武周之眾攻陷石州，殺刺史王儉。

translations.literal: By this time Jizhen and his younger brother Liu'er again raised troops in rebellion, brought Liu Wuzhou's forces to attack and capture Shi Prefecture, and killed the prefect Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jizhen and his younger brother Liu'er rose again in rebellion, brought Liu Wuzhou's army against Shi Prefecture, took the city, and killed the prefect Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 季真自稱突利可汗，以六兒為拓定王。

translations.literal: Jizhen styled himself Khagan Tuli and made Liu'er Prince of Tuoding.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen declared himself Khagan Tuli and made Liu'er Prince of Tuoding.

sentences.zh: 六兒隋使請降，詔以為嵐州總管。

translations.literal: Liu'er sent a Sui envoy to request surrender; an edict appointed him regional commander of Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu'er sent envoys to the Sui court to surrender. An edict appointed him regional commander of Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以秦王世民為左武候大將軍、使持節、涼、甘等九州諸軍事、涼州總管，其太尉、尚書令、雍州牧、陝東道行台並如故。

translations.literal: On the day Renwu the Prince of Qin Shimin was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the nine prefectures of Liang, Gan, and others, and regional commander of Liang Prefecture; his posts as Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Governor of Yong Prefecture, and Eastern Shaanxi Circuit Commissioner remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renwu, Prince of Qin Shimin was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, commander of military affairs for the nine prefectures including Liang and Gan, and regional commander of Liang Prefecture. His existing posts as Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Governor of Yong Prefecture, and Eastern Shaanxi Circuit Commissioner were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遣黃門侍郎楊恭仁安撫河西。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Gongren was sent to pacify the Hexi region.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was dispatched to pacify the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，劉武周陷平遙。

translations.literal: On the day Bingxu, Liu Wuzhou captured Pingyao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingxu, Liu Wuzhou took Pingyao.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，梁州總管、山東道安撫副使陳政為麾下所殺，攜其首奔王世充。

translations.literal: On the day Guisi, Chen Zheng, regional commander of Liang Prefecture and Vice Commissioner for Pacification of the Shandong Circuit, was killed by his subordinates, who carried off his head and fled to Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guisi, Chen Zheng, regional commander of Liang and Vice Commissioner for Pacification of the Shandong Circuit, was murdered by his own troops. They carried off his head and fled to Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 政，茂之子也。

translations.literal: Zheng was the son of Chen Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zheng was the son of Chen Mao.

sentences.zh: 王世充以禮部尚書裴仁基、左輔大將軍裴行儼有威名，忌之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, because the Minister of Rites Pei Renji and the Left Assistant Grand General Pei Xingyan had renown and prestige, was jealous of them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was jealous of Minister of Rites Pei Renji and Left Assistant Grand General Pei Xingyan, both men of great reputation.

sentences.zh: 仁基父子知之，亦不自安，乃與尚書左丞宇文儒童、儒童弟尚食直長溫、散騎常侍崔德本謀殺世充及其黨，復尊立皇泰主；

translations.literal: The father and son Renji knew this and were also ill at ease; they therefore joined with Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuwen Rutong, Rutong's younger brother the Chief of the Imperial Kitchen Wen, and Irregular Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Deben in a plot to kill Shichong and his faction and restore Emperor Yang Tong to honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Peis knew they were marked and grew uneasy. Together with Left Assistant Director Yuwen Rutong, Rutong's younger brother Wen of the Imperial Kitchen, and Irregular Attendant Cui Deben, they plotted to kill Shichong and his followers and restore Emperor Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 事洩，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out, and all three generations of their families were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered, and three generations of every family involved were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 齊王世惲言於世充曰：「儒童等謀反，正為皇泰主尚在故也，不如早除之。」

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Shi Yun said to Shichong, "Rutong and the others plotted rebellion precisely because Emperor Yang Tong is still alive—better to remove him early."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Shi Yun told Shichong, "Rutong and the others rebelled because Emperor Yang Tong is still alive. Better to get rid of him now."

sentences.zh: 世充從之，遣兄子唐王仁則及家奴梁百年鴆皇泰主。

translations.literal: Shichong followed this advice and sent his elder brother's son Prince of Tang Ren Ze and the household slave Liang Bainian to poison Emperor Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong agreed and sent his nephew Prince of Tang Ren Ze and the household slave Liang Bainian to poison Emperor Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主曰：「更為請太尉，以往者之言，未應至此。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yang Tong said, "Please ask the Grand Marshal again—for what was said before, it ought not to have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang Tong said, "Ask the Grand Marshal again for me. Given what he promised before, it should never have come to this."

sentences.zh: 百年欲為啟陳，世惲不許；

translations.literal: Bainian wished to go and report this, but Shi Yun would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian wanted to relay the message, but Shi Yun refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 又請與皇太后辭決，亦不許。

translations.literal: He again requested to take leave of the Empress Dowager, but this too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked once more to bid farewell to the Empress Dowager, and that too was refused.

sentences.zh: 乃布度焚香禮佛：「願自今已往，不復生帝王家！」

translations.literal: Then he spread a mat, burned incense, and paid homage to the Buddha, saying: "From this day forward, may I never again be born into an imperial house!"
translations.idiomatic: He spread a mat, lit incense, and prayed before the Buddha: "May I never again be born into a ruler's house, from this day on!"

sentences.zh: 飲藥，不能絕，以帛縊殺之。

translations.literal: He drank the poison, but it did not kill him; they strangled him with silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison, but it failed to end his life, so they strangled him with a silk cord.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭皇帝。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 世充以其兄楚王世偉為太保，齊王世惲為太傅，領尚書令。

translations.literal: Shichong appointed his elder brother, Prince of Chu Wang Wei, as Grand Guardian, and Prince of Qi Wang Yun as Grand Tutor, who also held the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong made his elder brother, Prince of Chu Wang Wei, Grand Guardian, and Prince of Qi Wang Yun Grand Tutor and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，竇建德陷滄州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengzi, Dou Jiande captured Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day gengzi, Dou Jiande took Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，易州賊帥宋金剛，有眾萬餘，與魏刀兒連結。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Jingang, the bandit chief of Yizhou, had forces of more than ten thousand and was allied with Wei Dao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Jingang, a rebel leader in Yizhou, commanded more than ten thousand men and was allied with Wei Dao'er.

sentences.zh: 刀兒為竇建德所滅，金剛救之，戰敗，帥眾四千西奔劉武周，武周聞其善用兵，得之，甚喜，號曰宋王，委以軍事，中分家貲以遺之。

translations.literal: When Dao'er was destroyed by Dou Jiande, Jingang went to rescue him but was defeated; he led four thousand men west to join Liu Wuzhou. Wuzhou, hearing that Jingang was skilled in warfare, was greatly pleased to obtain him, titled him King of Song, entrusted him with military affairs, and gave him half his family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao'er was wiped out by Dou Jiande, Jingang marched to his relief but was beaten; he led four thousand men west to Liu Wuzhou. Wuzhou, who had heard of Jingang's skill in war, was delighted to have him, named him King of Song, put him in charge of the army, and gave him half his household goods.

sentences.zh: 金剛亦深自結，出其故妻，納武周之妹，因說武周圖晉陽，南向爭天下。

translations.literal: Jingang also formed a deep bond with him: he set aside his former wife and married Wuzhou's sister, and thereby persuaded Wuzhou to scheme against Jinyang and march south to contend for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang bound himself closely to Wuzhou as well—he dismissed his former wife, took Wuzhou's sister in marriage, and urged Wuzhou to seize Jinyang and march south to fight for the empire.

sentences.zh: 武周以金剛為西南道大行台，使將兵三萬寇并州。

translations.literal: Wuzhou made Jingang Grand Marshal of the Southwest Circuit and sent him with thirty thousand troops to raid Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou appointed Jingang Grand Marshal of the Southwest Circuit and sent him with thirty thousand troops to invade Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，武周進逼介州，沙門道澄以佛幡縋之入城，遂陷介州；

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Wuzhou pressed close to Jiezhou; the monk Daocheng was lowered into the city on a Buddhist banner, and thus they captured Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Wuzhou advanced on Jiezhou; the monk Daocheng was let down into the city on a Buddhist pennant, and Jiezhou fell.

sentences.zh: 詔左武衛大將軍姜寶誼、行軍總管李仲文擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Left Martial Guard General Jiang Baoyi and the campaigning commander Li Zhongwen to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Left Martial Guard General Jiang Baoyi and campaigning commander Li Zhongwen to strike him.

sentences.zh: 武周將黃子英往來雀鼠谷，數以輕兵挑戰，兵才接，子英陽不勝而走，如是再三，寶宜、仲文悉眾逐之，伏兵發，唐兵大敗，寶誼、仲文皆為所虜。

translations.literal: Wuzhou's general Huang Ziying moved back and forth through Queque Valley, repeatedly provoking with light troops; as soon as the armies engaged, Ziying would feign defeat and flee. After this happened several times, Baoyi and Zhongwen pursued with their full forces; ambush troops sprang up and the Tang army was routed; both Baoyi and Zhongwen were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou's general Huang Ziying ranged through Queque Valley, again and again drawing them out with light troops; as soon as battle was joined, Ziying would pretend to lose and withdraw. After this happened several times, Baoyi and Zhongwen gave chase with their entire force; the ambush closed in, the Tang army was shattered, and both Baoyi and Zhongwen were taken.

sentences.zh: 既而俱逃歸，上復使二人將兵擊武周。

translations.literal: Before long both escaped and returned; the Emperor again sent the two men to lead troops against Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both men escaped and returned; the Emperor again sent them out against Wuzhou at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 己酉，突厥遣使來告始畢可汗之喪，上舉哀於長樂門，廢朝三日，詔百官就館吊其使者。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, the Turks sent envoys to announce the death of Qaghan Shibi; the Emperor mourned at Chang Le Gate, suspended court for three days, and ordered all officials to go to the envoys' lodge to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, the Turks sent envoys to announce the death of Qaghan Shibi; the Emperor mourned at Chang Le Gate, suspended court for three days, and ordered every official to call at the envoys' quarters to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 又遣內史舍人鄭德挺吊處羅可汗，賻帛三萬段。

translations.literal: He also sent the Palace Secretariat drafting attendant Zheng Deting to mourn Qaghan Chuluo, with thirty thousand bolts of condolence silks.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Palace Secretariat drafting attendant Zheng Deting to mourn Qaghan Chuluo, with thirty thousand bolts of funeral silks.

sentences.zh: 上以劉武周入寇為憂，右僕射裴寂請自行。

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled by Liu Wuzhou's invasion; the Right Vice Director Pei Ji requested to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was anxious over Liu Wuzhou's invasion, and Right Vice Director Pei Ji asked to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以寂為晉州道行軍總管，討武周，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Ji was made campaigning commander of the Jinzhou circuit to suppress Wuzhou, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, Ji was appointed campaigning commander of the Jinzhou circuit to suppress Wuzhou, with full discretion to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，初置十二軍，分關內諸府以隸焉，皆取天星為名，以車騎府統之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Twelve Armies were first established; the prefectures within Guanzhong were apportioned to belong to them, each named after a celestial star, and the Chariots and Cavalry Directorate was placed over them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Twelve Armies were first established; the Guanzhong prefectures were divided among them, each army taking the name of a star, all under the Chariots and Cavalry Directorate.

sentences.zh: 每軍將、副各一人，取威名素重者為之，督以耕戰之務。

translations.literal: Each army had one commander and one deputy, chosen from men of established renown, who were charged with both farming and fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one commander and one deputy, drawn from men of long-standing reputation, and charged with both farming and fighting.

sentences.zh: 由是士馬精強，所向無敵。

translations.literal: From this the troops and horses were elite and strong, and none could withstand them wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: From this the men and horses grew keen and strong, and they met no equal wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 海岱賊帥徐圓朗以數州之地請降，拜兗州總管，封魯國公。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang, the bandit chief of the Haiai region, offered submission with several prefectures and was appointed Grand Commander of Yanzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang, a rebel leader on the Haiai coast, submitted several prefectures and was made Grand Commander of Yanzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 王世充遣其將羅士信寇穀州，士信帥其眾千餘人來降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent his general Luo Shixin to raid Guzhou; Shixin led more than a thousand of his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his general Luo Shixin to raid Guzhou, but Shixin led more than a thousand of his men over to the Tang side.

sentences.zh: 先是，士信從李密擊世充，兵敗，為世充所得，世充厚禮之，與同寢食。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shixin had followed Li Mi in attacking Shichong but was defeated and captured by Shichong, who treated him generously and shared bed and board with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shixin had followed Li Mi against Shichong, was beaten, and fell into Shichong's hands; Shichong treated him handsomely and even shared his bed and meals with him.

sentences.zh: 既而得邴元真等，待之如士信，士信恥之。

translations.literal: Later, when Shichong obtained Xing Yuanzhen and others, he treated them the same as Shixin, which Shixin found shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shichong took Xing Yuanzhen and others prisoner, he treated them no differently than Shixin, which Shixin found humiliating.

sentences.zh: 士信有駿馬，世充兄子趙王道詢欲之，不與，世充奪之以賜道詢；

translations.literal: Shixin had a fine steed; Wang Shichong's nephew, Prince of Zhao Wang Daoxun, wanted it but was refused, so Shichong seized it and gave it to Daoxun.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin owned a fine horse; Shichong's nephew, Prince of Zhao Wang Daoxun, wanted it, but Shixin would not give it up, so Shichong seized the horse and bestowed it on Daoxun.

sentences.zh: 士信怒，故來降。

translations.literal: Shixin was angry and therefore came over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin was enraged, and that is why he defected.

sentences.zh: 上聞其來，甚喜，遣使迎勞，賜帛五千段，稟食其所部，以士信為陝州道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of his arrival he was greatly pleased, sent envoys to welcome and reward him, granted five thousand bolts of silk, supplied provisions for his troops, and appointed Shixin campaigning commander of the Shanzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard he had come, he was delighted, sent envoys to welcome and reward him, granted five thousand bolts of silk, supplied rations for his troops, and made Shixin campaigning commander of the Shanzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 世充左龍驤將軍臨涇席辯與同列楊虔安、李君義皆帥所部來降。

translations.literal: Shichong's Left Dragon-soaring General Xi Bian of Linjing, along with his colleagues Yang Qian'an and Li Junyi, all led their units to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's Left Dragon-soaring General Xi Bian of Linjing, together with his fellows Yang Qian'an and Li Junyi, each led his command across in surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙子，王世充遣其將郭士衡寇穀州，刺史任瑰大破之，俘斬且盡。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Wang Shichong sent his general Guo Shiheng to raid Guzhou; the prefect Ren Gui routed them utterly, capturing and killing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Wang Shichong sent his general Guo Shiheng against Guzhou; Prefect Ren Gui crushed the force and captured or killed nearly every man.

sentences.zh: 甲申，行軍總管劉弘基遣其將種如願襲王世充河陽城，毀其河橋而還。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the campaigning commander Liu Hongji sent his general Zhong Ruyuan to strike Wang Shichong's Heye City, destroy the river bridge, and return.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, campaigning commander Liu Hongji sent his general Zhong Ruyuan to raid Wang Shichong's Heye City, destroy the river bridge, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，西突厥統葉護可汗、高昌王麴伯雅各遣使入貢。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Qaghan Tong Yehu of the Western Turks and King Qu Boke of Gaochang each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Qaghan Tong Yehu of the Western Turks and King Qu Boke of Gaochang each sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥曷娑那可汗入朝於隋，隋人留之，國人立其叔父，號射匱可汗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qaghan Yasa of the Western Turks had gone to court at the Sui; the Sui detained him, and his countrymen enthroned his uncle, titled Qaghan Shegui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qaghan Yasa of the Western Turks had gone to the Sui court; the Sui kept him there, and his people enthroned his uncle as Qaghan Shegui.

sentences.zh: 射匱者，達頭可汗之孫也，既立，拓地東至金山，西至海，遂與北突厥為敵，建庭於龜茲北三彌山。

translations.literal: Shegui was the grandson of Qaghan Datou; once established, he extended his territory east to Jinshan and west to the sea, became the rival of the Northern Turks, and established his court north of Kucha at Mount Sanmi.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui was a grandson of Qaghan Datou; once enthroned, he pushed his borders east to Jinshan and west to the sea, made an enemy of the Northern Turks, and set his court north of Kucha at Mount Sanmi.

sentences.zh: 射匱卒，弟統葉護立。

translations.literal: Shegui died, and his younger brother Tong Yehu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shegui died, his younger brother Tong Yehu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 統葉護勇而有謀，北並鐵勒，控弦數十萬，據烏孫故地，又移庭於石國北千泉；

translations.literal: Tong Yehu was brave and resourceful; he merged with the Tiele in the north, commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, held the old lands of the Wusun, and moved his court again to Qianquan north of Shiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu was bold and shrewd; he absorbed the Tiele in the north, commanded several hundred thousand archers, held the old Wusun lands, and moved his court again to Qianquan, north of Shiguo.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國皆臣之，葉護各遣吐屯監之，督其徵賦。

translations.literal: All the states of the Western Regions submitted to him; Yehu sent tudun supervisors to each to oversee their levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Every state of the Western Regions submitted to him; Yehu sent a tudun overseer to each one to supervise levies and taxes.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋金剛寇浩州，浹旬而退。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Song Jingang raided Haozhou and withdrew after ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, Song Jingang raided Haozhou and withdrew after ten days of fighting.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁酉，酅公薨，謚曰隋恭帝；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day dingyou, the Duke of Xi passed away; his posthumous title was Emperor Gong of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day dingyou, the Duke of Xi died; he was given the posthumous title Emperor Gong of Sui.

sentences.zh: 無後，以族子行基嗣。

translations.literal: Having no heirs, his clansman Xingji was made successor.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so his clansman Xingji was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 竇建德將兵十餘萬趣洺州，淮安王神通帥諸軍退保相州。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande marched with more than a hundred thousand troops toward Mingzhou; Prince Huai'an Li Shentong led the armies in retreat to defend Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande advanced on Mingzhou with more than a hundred thousand men; Prince Huai'an Li Shentong drew the armies back to hold Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，建德兵至洺州城下。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Jiande's troops reached the walls of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, Jiande's army came up to the walls of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，將軍秦武通軍至洛陽，敗王世充將葛彥璋。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, General Qin Wutong's army reached Luoyang and defeated Wang Shichong's general Ge Yanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu, General Qin Wutong's army reached Luoyang and defeated Wang Shichong's general Ge Yanzhang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，竇建德陷洺州，總管袁子幹降之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Dou Jiande captured Mingzhou; the commander Yuan Zigian surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Dou Jiande took Mingzhou; Commander Yuan Zigian surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，引兵趣相州，淮安王神通聞之。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Jiande led his troops toward Xiangzhou; Prince Huai'an Shentong heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, Jiande marched toward Xiangzhou; Prince Huai'an Shentong heard the news.

sentences.zh: 帥諸軍就李世勣於黎陽。

translations.literal: He led the armies to join Li Shiji at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He led the armies to join Li Shiji at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 梁師都與突厥命數千騎寇延州，行軍總管段德操兵少不敵，閉壁不戰，伺師都稍怠，九月，丙寅，遣副總管梁禮將兵擊之。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu, at the Turks' command, raided Yanzhou with several thousand horsemen. The campaigning commander Duan Decao had too few troops to match them and shut the walls without fighting, waiting until Shidu slackened somewhat; in the ninth month, on the day bingyin, he sent Vice Commander Liang Li with troops to strike.
translations.idiomatic: At the Turks' bidding, Liang Shidu raided Yanzhou with several thousand horsemen. Campaigning commander Duan Decao had too few men to meet them and shut the walls without giving battle, watching until Shidu grew careless; in the ninth month, on the day bingyin, he sent Vice Commander Liang Li out to attack.

sentences.zh: 師都與禮戰方酣，德操以輕騎多張旗幟，掩擊其後，師都軍潰；

translations.literal: While Shidu and Li were locked in fierce battle, Decao led light cavalry with many banners in a flanking attack from the rear; Shidu's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: While Shidu and Li were locked in fierce combat, Decao swept around the rear with light cavalry flying many banners; Shidu's army broke.

sentences.zh: 逐北二百餘里，破其魏州，虜男女二千餘口。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy more than two hundred li, took his Wei prefecture, and captured more than two thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the fugitives more than two hundred li, seized his Wei prefecture, and took more than two thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 德操，孝先之子也。

translations.literal: Decao was the son of Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Decao was the son of Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑遣其將楊道生寇峽州，剌史許紹擊破之。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian sent his general Yang Daosheng to raid Xiazhou; the prefect Xu Shao routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian sent his general Yang Daosheng against Xiazhou; Prefect Xu Shao drove him off.

sentences.zh: 銑又遣其將陳普環帥舟師上峽，規取巴、蜀。

translations.literal: Xian also sent his general Chen Puhuan leading a fleet up the gorge, planning to seize Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also sent his general Chen Puhuan up the gorge with a fleet, intending to take Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 紹遣其子智仁及錄事參軍李弘節等追至西陵，大破之，擒普環。

translations.literal: Shao sent his son Zhiren and the recording secretary Li Hongjie and others in pursuit to Xiling, where they inflicted a great defeat and captured Puhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent his son Zhiren and recording secretary Li Hongjie and others in pursuit to Xiling, where they won a crushing victory and captured Puhuan.

sentences.zh: 銑遣兵戍安蜀城及荊門城。

translations.literal: Xian sent troops to garrison Ancheng and Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent troops to garrison Ancheng and Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 先是，上遣開府李靖詣夔州經略蕭銑。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had sent the Defender-Lieutenant Li Jing to Kuizhou to deal with Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Emperor had sent Defender-Lieutenant Li Jing to Kuizhou to deal with Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 靖至峽州，阻銑兵，久不得進。

translations.literal: Jing reached Xiazhou but was blocked by Xian's troops and for a long time could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reached Xiazhou but was blocked by Xian's troops and could not advance for a long time.

sentences.zh: 上怒其遲留，陰敕許紹斬之；

translations.literal: The Emperor, angry at his delay, secretly ordered Xu Shao to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, furious at the delay, secretly ordered Xu Shao to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 紹惜其才，為之奏請，獲免。

translations.literal: Shao valued his talent and memorialized on his behalf; Jing was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shao prized his ability and pleaded for him in a memorial; Jing was spared.

sentences.zh: 己巳，竇建德陷相州，殺刺史呂鈱。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Dou Jiande captured Xiangzhou and killed the prefect Lu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi, Dou Jiande took Xiangzhou and killed Prefect Lu Yin.

sentences.zh: 民部尚書魯公劉文靜，自以才略功勳在裴寂之右，而位居其下，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing, Duke of Lu and Minister of Revenue, considered his talent, stratagem, and achievements to surpass Pei Ji's, yet his rank was below Ji's, and he was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing, Duke of Lu and Minister of Revenue, believed his talent, strategy, and achievements outstripped Pei Ji's, yet he stood below him in rank, and he was deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 每廷議，寂有所是，文靜必非之，數侵侮寂，由是有隙。

translations.literal: At every court discussion, whatever Ji endorsed Wenjing would oppose; he repeatedly insulted Ji, and thus a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: At every court debate, whatever Ji approved Wenjing opposed; he insulted Ji again and again, and a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 文靜與弟通直散騎常侍文起飲，酒酣，怨望，拔刀擊柱曰：「會當斬裴寂首！」

translations.literal: Wenjing drank with his younger brother, the Palace Attendant-attending Regular Wen Qi; when drunk he vented his grievances, drew his sword and struck a pillar, saying: "I shall surely take Pei Ji's head one day!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing drank with his younger brother, Palace Attendant-attending Regular Wen Qi; deep in his cups he gave vent to his bitterness, drew his sword, and struck a pillar, crying, "One day I shall take Pei Ji's head!"

sentences.zh: 家數有妖，文起召巫於星下被發銜刀為厭勝。

translations.literal: There had been several omens in the household; Wen Qi summoned a shaman under the stars, with hair unbound and a knife in his mouth, to perform apotropaic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Several uncanny signs had appeared in the house; Wen Qi summoned a shaman beneath the stars, hair loose and a knife held in his mouth, to perform rites of exorcism.

sentences.zh: 文靜有妾無寵，使其兄上變告之。

translations.literal: Wenjing had a concubine who was out of favor; he had her brother lodge an accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing had a concubine who had fallen from favor; he had her brother bring a denunciation against him.

sentences.zh: 上以文靜屬吏，遣裴寂、蕭瑀問狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor turned Wenjing over to the law officers and sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor handed Wenjing over to the judicial officers and sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to question him.

sentences.zh: 文靜曰：「建義之初，忝為司馬，計與長史位望略同。

translations.literal: Wenjing said: "At the founding of the righteous cause I was honored as Army Marshal; my standing was roughly equal to that of the Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said, "At the founding of our cause I served as Army Marshal, and my standing was roughly on a par with the Chief Clerk's.

sentences.zh: 今寂為僕射，據甲第；

translations.literal: Now Ji is Vice Director and occupies a grand mansion;
translations.idiomatic: Now Ji is Vice Director and lives in a great mansion;

sentences.zh: 臣官賞不異眾人，東西征討，老母留京師，風雨無所庇，實有觖望之心，因醉怨言，不能自保。」

translations.literal: my rank and rewards are no different from the common crowd. Campaigning east and west while my aged mother remains in the capital with no shelter from wind and rain — I truly harbored resentment; in my cups I uttered complaints and could not restrain myself."
translations.idiomatic: my rank and rewards are no better than anyone else's. I have campaigned east and west while my aged mother stayed in the capital with no roof over her head in wind and rain — I did harbor resentment; drunk, I spoke bitterly and could not hold my tongue."

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「觀文靜此言，反明白矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the assembled ministers: "Judging from Wenjing's words, his rebellion is clear."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the assembled ministers, "From Wenjing's own words, his treason is plain."

sentences.zh: 李綱、蕭瑀皆明其不反，秦王世民為之固請曰：「昔在晉陽，文靜先定非常之策，始告寂知；

translations.literal: Li Gang and Xiao Yu both made clear that he had not rebelled; Prince of Qin Shimin earnestly pleaded on his behalf, saying: "Long ago at Jinyang, Wenjing first devised the extraordinary plan and only then informed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang and Xiao Yu both declared that he had not rebelled; Prince of Qin Shimin pleaded earnestly for him, saying, "Long ago at Jinyang, Wenjing was the first to settle on the extraordinary plan and only then told Ji.

sentences.zh: 及克京城，任遇懸隔，令文靜觖望則有之，非敢謀反。」

translations.literal: When the capital was taken, his appointment and treatment were far apart — it may well have made Wenjing resentful, but he does not dare to plot rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was taken, his treatment and Ji’s were worlds apart — that may have bred resentment in Wenjing, but he does not dare plot rebellion."

sentences.zh: 裴寂言於上曰：「文靜才略實冠時人，性復粗險，今天下未定，留之必貽後患。」

translations.literal: Pei Ji said to the Emperor: "Wenjing's talent and stratagem truly surpass all men of the age, and his nature is moreover rough and dangerous; with the realm not yet settled, keeping him would surely bring later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji said to the Emperor, "Wenjing's talent and strategy truly surpass every man of the age, and his nature is rough and treacherous besides; with the realm not yet settled, sparing him will surely breed trouble later."

sentences.zh: 上素親寂，低回久之，卒用寂言。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long been close to Ji; he deliberated at length and finally adopted Ji's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long been close to Ji; he hesitated a long while, but in the end he took Ji's advice.

sentences.zh: 辛未，文靜及文起坐死，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Wenjing and Wen Qi were executed and their households confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Wenjing and Wen Qi were put to death and their families' property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 沈法興既克毘陵，謂江、淮之南指摠可定，自稱梁王，都毘陵，改元延康，置百官。

translations.literal: After Shen Faxing captured Piling, he believed the lands south of the Yangzi and Huai could be settled at a gesture; he styled himself King of Liang, made Piling his capital, changed the era name to Yankang, and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Faxing took Piling, he believed the lands south of the Yangzi and Huai could be won at a wave of the hand; he declared himself King of Liang, made Piling his capital, adopted the era name Yankang, and set up a full court.

sentences.zh: 性殘忍，專尚威刑，將士小有過，即斬之，由是其下離怨。

translations.literal: He was cruel by nature and relied solely on harsh punishments; officers and soldiers who committed the slightest fault were beheaded at once, and thus his followers grew alienated and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel by nature and trusted only terror; the slightest fault in an officer or soldier meant instant execution, and his men grew estranged and bitter.

sentences.zh: 時杜伏威據歷陽，陳稜據江都，李子通據海陵，俱有窺江表之心。

translations.literal: At that time Du Fuwei held Liyang, Chen Ling held Jiangdu, and Li Zitong held Hailing; each harbored designs on the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Fuwei held Liyang, Chen Ling held Jiangdu, and Li Zitong held Hailing; each cast a covetous eye on the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 法興軍數敗；

translations.literal: Faxing's armies suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing's armies suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 會子通圍稜於江都，稜送質求救於法興及伏威，法興使其子綸將兵數萬，與伏威共救之。

translations.literal: When Zitong besieged Ling at Jiangdu, Ling sent hostages to beg rescue from Faxing and Fuwei; Faxing sent his son Lun with tens of thousands of troops to join Fuwei in the relief effort.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zitong besieged Ling at Jiangdu; Ling sent hostages to beg Faxing and Fuwei for aid, and Faxing sent his son Lun with tens of thousands of men to join Fuwei in the rescue.

sentences.zh: 伏威軍清流，綸軍揚子，相去數十里。

translations.literal: Fuwei encamped at Qingliu and Lun at Yangzi, several dozen li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei camped at Qingliu and Lun at Yangzi, several dozen li apart.

sentences.zh: 子通納言毛文深獻策，募江南人詐為綸兵，夜襲伏威營，伏威怒，復遣兵襲綸。

translations.literal: Zitong's Director of Protocol Mao Wenshen proposed a stratagem: recruit men from south of the Yangzi to impersonate Lun's troops and raid Fuwei's camp by night. Fuwei was enraged and in turn sent troops to attack Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's Director of Protocol Mao Wenshen offered a plan: hire men from south of the Yangzi to pose as Lun's soldiers and raid Fuwei's camp by night. Fuwei was furious and sent troops against Lun in return.

sentences.zh: 由是二人相疑，莫敢先進。

translations.literal: From this the two men grew suspicious of each other, and none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: From this the two men grew suspicious of each other, and neither dared move first.

sentences.zh: 子通得盡銳攻江都，克之，稜奔伏威。

translations.literal: Zitong was thus able to throw his full strength against Jiangdu, took it, and Ling fled to Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong was thus able to throw his full strength against Jiangdu, took the city, and Ling fled to Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 子通入江都，因縱擊綸，大破之，伏威亦引去。

translations.literal: Zitong entered Jiangdu and then turned to strike Lun, routing him decisively; Fuwei also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong entered Jiangdu and then turned on Lun, crushing him; Fuwei withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 子通即皇帝位，國號吳，改元明政。

translations.literal: Zitong immediately assumed the imperial title; his state was called Wu and the era name Mingzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong thereupon took the imperial title; his state was called Wu and the era name Mingzheng.

sentences.zh: 丹楊賊帥樂伯通帥眾萬餘降之，子通以為左僕射。

translations.literal: Yue Botong, the bandit chief of Danyang, led more than ten thousand men to submit; Zitong made him Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Botong, a rebel leader in Danyang, brought more than ten thousand men over to him; Zitong made him Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威請降；

translations.literal: Du Fuwei requested to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei offered to submit.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以伏威為淮南安撫大使、和州總管。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Fuwei was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Huainan and Grand Commander of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Fuwei was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Huainan and Grand Commander of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 裴寂至介休，宋金剛據城拒之。

translations.literal: Pei Ji reached Jiexiu; Song Jingang held the city and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji reached Jiexiu, but Song Jingang held the city against him.

sentences.zh: 寂軍於度索原，營中飲澗水，金剛絕之，士卒渴乏。

translations.literal: Ji camped at Dusuo Plain; the camp drank stream water, but Jingang cut it off and the soldiers were parched and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Ji encamped at Dusuo Plain; his men drank from the stream, but Jingang cut off the water and the troops were left thirsty and spent.

sentences.zh: 寂欲移營就水，金剛縱兵擊之，寂軍遂潰，失亡略盡，寂一日一夜馳至晉州。

translations.literal: Ji wished to move camp to reach water; Jingang loosed his troops upon him and Ji's army collapsed, with losses nearly total; Ji rode day and night to reach Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji tried to shift camp toward water; Jingang unleashed his troops on him, and Ji's army broke; losses were nearly total, and Ji rode day and night to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉武周屢遣兵攻西河，浩州剌史劉贍拒之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Wuzhou had repeatedly sent troops to attack Xihe; Liu Shan, prefect of Haozhou, held them off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Wuzhou had repeatedly sent troops against Xihe; Liu Shan, prefect of Haozhou, held them off.

sentences.zh: 李仲文引兵就之，與共守西河。

translations.literal: Li Zhongwen led his troops to join him, and together they defended Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongwen marched to join him, and together they held Xihe.

sentences.zh: 及裴寂敗，自晉州以北城鎮俱沒，唯西河獨存。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji was defeated, every walled town north of Jinzhou fell — only Xihe remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji was beaten, every walled town north of Jinzhou fell — only Xihe still stood.

sentences.zh: 姜寶誼復為金剛所虜，謀逃歸，金剛殺之。

translations.literal: Jiang Baoyi was again captured by Jingang; when he plotted escape Jingang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Baoyi was captured by Jingang again; when he tried to escape and return, Jingang put him to death.

sentences.zh: 裴寂上表謝罪，上慰諭之，復使鎮撫河東。

translations.literal: Pei Ji submitted a memorial accepting blame; the Emperor comforted him and again entrusted him with pacifying Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji submitted a memorial accepting blame; the Emperor comforted him and again put him in charge of pacifying Hedong.

sentences.zh: 劉武周進逼并州，齊王元吉紿其司馬劉德威曰：「卿以老弱守城，吾以強兵出戰。」

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou pressed close to Bingzhou; Prince of Qi Yuanji deceived his Army Marshal Liu Dewei, saying: "You shall hold the city with the old and weak; I shall take the strong troops out to fight."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou advanced on Bingzhou; Prince of Qi Yuanji deceived his Army Marshal Liu Dewei, saying, "You hold the city with the old and the weak; I will take the crack troops out to fight."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，元吉夜出兵，攜其妻妾棄州奔還長安。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Yuanji marched out by night but abandoned the prefecture with his wives and concubines and fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Yuanji marched out by night, but with his wives and concubines in tow he abandoned the prefecture and fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 元吉始去，武周兵已至城下，晉陽土豪薛深以城納武周。

translations.literal: Yuanji had scarcely departed when Wuzhou's troops were already at the walls; the great clansman of Jinyang Xue Shen surrendered the city to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji had barely left when Wuzhou's troops were already at the walls; Xue Shen, a powerful man of Jinyang, handed the city over to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大怒，謂禮部尚書李綱曰：「元吉幼弱，未習時事，故遣竇誕、宇文歆輔之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he was furious and said to the Minister of Rites Li Gang: "Yuanji is young and inexperienced in affairs of state; that is why I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard the news he was furious and said to Minister of Rites Li Gang, "Yuanji is young and has not yet learned how to handle affairs; that is why I sent Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin to guide him.

sentences.zh: 晉陽強兵數萬，食支十年，興王之基，一旦棄之。

translations.literal: Jinyang had tens of thousands of elite troops and provisions enough for ten years—the very foundation upon which a royal house might be raised—and he threw it all away in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang held tens of thousands of crack troops and grain enough to last ten years—the foundation of an empire—and in one stroke he abandoned it all.

sentences.zh: 聞宇文歆首畫此策，我當斬之！」

translations.literal: I hear Yuwen Xin was the first to devise this plan—I ought to execute him!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear Yuwen Xin was first to counsel this course. I ought to have him executed!"

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「王年少驕逸，竇誕曾無規諫，又掩覆之，使士民憤怨，今日之敗，誕之罪也。

translations.literal: Gang said: "The prince is young, arrogant, and dissolute. Dou Yan never once remonstrated with him, but instead covered up his faults, causing officers and common people alike to seethe with resentment. Today's defeat is Yan's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang replied, "The prince is young, arrogant, and unrestrained. Dou Yan never offered honest counsel; instead he covered up his faults until soldiers and civilians boiled with resentment. Today's defeat is Yan's fault.

sentences.zh: 歆諫，王不悛，尋皆聞奏，乃忠臣也，豈可殺哉！」

translations.literal: Xin remonstrated, yet the prince would not repent; soon all his advice was reported to the throne—he is a loyal minister. How could he be killed!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin did remonstrate, but the prince would not mend his ways; Xin soon had all his remonstrances reported upward. He is a loyal minister—how could Your Majesty put him to death!"

sentences.zh: 明日，上召綱入，升御座曰：「我得公，遂無濫刑。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned Gang and, mounting the imperial throne, said: "Having obtained you, I am spared indiscriminate punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor summoned Gang in, ascended the throne, and said, "Once I had you at court, I was spared the abuse of capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 元吉自為不善，非二人所能禁也。」

translations.literal: Yuanji brings evil on himself—two men could not have restrained him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brought this ruin on himself; two men could not have held him in check."

sentences.zh: 並誕赦之。

translations.literal: And he pardoned both Dou Yan and him.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned both Dou Yan and Yuwen Xin.

sentences.zh: 衛尉少卿劉政會在太原，為武周所虜，政會密遣人奉表論武周形勢。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan Liu Zhenghui was at Taiyuan and was captured by Wuzhou; Zhenghui secretly sent a man to submit a memorial analyzing Wuzhou's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan Liu Zhenghui was in Taiyuan when Liu Wuzhou took him prisoner; Zhenghui secretly sent an envoy to the capital with a memorial analyzing Wuzhou's military posture.

sentences.zh: 武周據太原，遣宋金剛攻晉州，拔之，虜右驍衛大將軍劉弘基，弘基逃歸。

translations.literal: Wuzhou held Taiyuan and sent Song Jingang to attack Jin Prefecture, took it, and captured General of the Right Majestic Cavalry Guards Liu Hongji; Hongji fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou held Taiyuan and sent Song Jingang against Jin Prefecture, which fell; he captured General Liu Hongji of the Right Majestic Cavalry Guards, though Hongji later escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 金剛進逼絳州，陷龍門。

translations.literal: Jingang pressed on toward Jiang Prefecture and captured Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang pressed forward toward Jiang Prefecture and took Longmen.

sentences.zh: 西突厥曷娑那可汗與北突厥有怨；

translations.literal: The Western Turkic khan Yeshana had a grievance against the Northern Turks;
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turkic khan Yeshana bore a grudge against the Northern Turks;

sentences.zh: 曷娑那在長安，北突厥遣使請殺之，上不許。

translations.literal: Yeshana was in Chang'an; the Northern Turks sent envoys requesting that he be killed, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yeshana had taken refuge in Chang'an. The Northern Turks sent envoys asking that he be put to death, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰：「保一人而失一國，後必為患！」

translations.literal: All the ministers said: "To preserve one man and lose a whole state—later this will surely become a calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said, "To spare one man and lose an entire kingdom—this will surely bring trouble later!"

sentences.zh: 秦王世民曰：「人窮來歸我，殺之不義。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Li Shimin said: "When a man in desperation comes to join us, to kill him is unjust."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, said, "A man at the end of his rope has come to seek our protection; to kill him would be wrong."

sentences.zh: 上遲回久之，不得己，丙戌，引曷娑那於內殿宴飲，既而送中書省，縱北突厥使者使殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor hesitated for a long time; having no choice, on day Bingxu he led Yeshana to a banquet in the inner hall, then sent him to the Secretariat and allowed the Northern Turkic envoys to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wavered for a long time, but at last, with no alternative, on the day Bingxu he entertained Yeshana at a feast in the inner palace, then handed him over to the Secretariat and let the Northern Turk envoys kill him.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李綱領太子詹事，太子建成始甚禮之。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Gang also served as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; the Crown Prince Jiancheng at first treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Gang also held the post of Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Crown Prince Jiancheng at first treated him with the utmost respect.

sentences.zh: 久之，太子漸暱近小人，疾秦王世民功高，頗相猜忌；

translations.literal: After a long while the Crown Prince gradually drew close to petty men, resented the Prince of Qin Li Shimin for his towering achievements, and grew mutually suspicious;
translations.idiomatic: In time the Crown Prince grew intimate with base companions, resented the Prince of Qin for his rising feats of arms, and became increasingly suspicious of him;

sentences.zh: 綱屢諫不聽，乃乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Gang repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded, and so requested his bones—that is, retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang remonstrated again and again without being heard, and finally asked to resign and retire.

sentences.zh: 上罵之曰：「卿為何潘仁長史，乃恥為朕尚書邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor berated him, saying: "You served Pan Ren as chief clerk—are you ashamed to be my Minister of Rites!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor scolded him: "You were chief clerk to Pan Ren—are you too ashamed to serve me as Minister of Rites!

sentences.zh: 且方使卿輔導建成，而固求去，何也？」

translations.literal: Moreover I am just about to have you guide and instruct Jiancheng, yet you obstinately seek to leave—why?"
translations.idiomatic: And I have only just appointed you to guide Jiancheng—yet you insist on leaving. Why?"

sentences.zh: 綱頓首曰：「潘仁，賊也，每欲妄殺人，臣諫之即止。

translations.literal: Gang bowed his head and said: "Pan Ren was a bandit who constantly wished to kill people wantonly; when I remonstrated he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang bowed low and said, "Pan Ren was a rebel who was always bent on killing innocent people at will; when I remonstrated with him, he ceased.

sentences.zh: 為其長史，可以無愧。

translations.literal: To have been his chief clerk—I can feel no shame.
translations.idiomatic: As his chief clerk I could serve without shame.

sentences.zh: 陛下創業明主，臣不才，所言如水投石，言於太子亦然，臣何敢久污天台，辱東朝乎！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a luminous sovereign who founded the dynasty; I am without talent—my words are like water cast upon stone; so too with the Crown Prince. How dare I long defile the imperial offices and disgrace the Eastern Palace!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a wise founding sovereign, but I am without talent; my words fall on deaf ears like water poured on stone—and the same is true with the Crown Prince. How dare I linger on to defile the imperial offices and bring disgrace upon the Eastern Palace!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「知公直士，勉留輔吾兒。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I know you are an upright man—do your best to stay and assist my son."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I know you are a man of integrity—please stay and guide my son."

sentences.zh: 戊子，以綱為太子少保，尚書、詹事如故。

translations.literal: On day Wuzi he appointed Gang Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with his posts as Minister and Grand Tutor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuzi he made Li Gang Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while retaining his posts as Minister of Rites and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 綱復上書諫太子飲酒無節，及信讒慝，疏骨肉。

translations.literal: Gang again submitted a memorial remonstrating that the Crown Prince drank without moderation, believed slander and wicked men, and kept his kin at arm's length.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang submitted another memorial warning the Crown Prince against intemperate drinking, trusting malicious slander, and estranging his own flesh and blood.

sentences.zh: 太子不懌，而所為如故。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was displeased, yet his conduct remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince took offense, but went on as before.

sentences.zh: 綱鬱鬱不得志，是歲，固稱老病辭職，詔解尚書，仍為少保。

translations.literal: Gang grew despondent and unfulfilled; that year he firmly pleaded old age and illness to resign; an edict relieved him of the Ministry but left him as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang languished in frustration. That year he pleaded age and illness to resign definitively; an edict relieved him of the ministry but left him as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通使慰撫使張道源鎮趙州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong had the pacification commissioner Zhang Daoyuan garrison Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong posted pacification commissioner Zhang Daoyuan to hold Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，竇建德陷趙州，執總管張志昂及道源。

translations.literal: On day Gengyin Dou Jiande took Zhao Prefecture and seized the commander Zhang Zhi'ang and Daoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengyin, Dou Jiande captured Zhao Prefecture and took commander Zhang Zhi'ang and Zhang Daoyuan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 建德以二人及邢州刺史陳君賓不早下，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Jiande wished to kill the two men and Xing Prefecture governor Chen Junbin for not having surrendered sooner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande wished to execute the two men along with Xing Prefecture governor Chen Junbin for failing to submit earlier.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒凌敬諫曰：「人臣各為其主用，彼堅守不下，乃忠臣也。

translations.literal: Chancellor of the National University Ling Jing remonstrated: "Each minister serves his own lord; they held firm and would not surrender—this is the conduct of loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the National University Ling Jing objected, "Every subject serves his own lord. Those men held their cities and refused to yield—that is the mark of loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 今大王殺之，何以勵群下乎！」

translations.literal: If Your Highness kills them now, how will you encourage your followers!"
translations.idiomatic: If you put loyal men to death, how will you inspire your followers!"

sentences.zh: 建德怒曰：「吾至城下，彼猶不降，力屈就擒，何可捨也！」

translations.literal: Jiande angrily said: "I came beneath their walls and still they would not surrender; only when their strength was spent did they submit to capture—how can they be spared!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande stormed, "I came to their walls and they still would not yield; only when their strength was gone did they let themselves be taken—how can I spare them!"

sentences.zh: 敬曰：「今大王使大將高士興拒羅藝於易水，藝才至，士興即降，大王之意以為何如？」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Your Highness lately sent the general Gao Shixing to hold Luo Yi at the Yi River; Yi had only just arrived when Shixing surrendered—what does Your Highness think of that?"
translations.idiomatic: Ling Jing said, "Not long ago you sent General Gao Shixing to hold Luo Yi at the Yi River. Yi had barely arrived when Shixing surrendered—what did you make of that?"

sentences.zh: 建德乃悟，即命釋之。

translations.literal: Jiande then understood and at once ordered them released.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande saw the point and immediately ordered them set free.

sentences.zh: 乙未，梁師都復寇延州，段德操擊破之，斬首二千餘級，師都以百餘騎遁去。

translations.literal: On day Yimou Liang Shidu again raided Yan Prefecture; Duan Decao defeated him and took more than two thousand heads; Shidu fled away with a little over a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yimou, Liang Shidu raided Yan Prefecture again; Duan Decao routed him, taking more than two thousand heads; Shidu fled with barely a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 德操以功拜柱國，賜爵平原郡公。

translations.literal: Decao was appointed pillar of the state for his merit and ennobled as Duke of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Decao was promoted to Pillar of the State for his achievement and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄜州刺史鄜城壯公梁禮戰沒。

translations.literal: Yan Prefecture governor the stalwart Duke of Yancheng Liang Li fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture governor Liang Li, Duke of Yancheng, died in battle.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，就加涼州總管楊恭仁納言；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day Jihai: Yang Gongren, regional commander of Liangzhou, was additionally appointed Master of Writings;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jihai, Yang Gongren, commander of Liangzhou, was additionally appointed Master of Writings;

sentences.zh: 賜幽州總管燕公羅藝姓李氏，封燕郡王。

translations.literal: Luo Yi, Duke of Yan and regional commander of Youzhou, was granted the surname Li and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi, Duke of Yan and commander of Youzhou, was granted the imperial surname Li and created Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，李藝破竇建德於衡水。

translations.literal: On day Xinchou Li Yi defeated Dou Jiande at Hengshui.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinchou, Li Yi defeated Dou Jiande at Hengshui.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以左武候大將軍龐玉為梁州總管。

translations.literal: On day Guimao Pang Yu, General of the Left Martial Guards, was made regional commander of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guimao, General Pang Yu of the Left Martial Guards was appointed commander of Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時集州獠反，玉討之，獠據險自守，軍不得進，糧且盡。

translations.literal: At that time the Liao of Ji Prefecture rebelled; Yu campaigned against them, but they held the defiles and would not yield; the army could not advance and provisions were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tribal peoples of Ji Prefecture rose in revolt; Yu marched against them, but they held the mountain passes and could not be dislodged; his army stalled and rations ran low.

sentences.zh: 熟獠與反者皆鄰里親黨，爭言賊不可擊，請玉還。

translations.literal: The pacified Liao and the rebels were all neighbors and kin; they all insisted the bandits could not be attacked and begged Yu to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The pacified tribesmen were neighbors and kinsmen of the rebels; they all insisted the enemy could not be beaten and begged Yu to turn back.

sentences.zh: 玉揚言：「秋谷將熟，百姓毋得收刈，一切供軍，非平賊吾不返。」

translations.literal: Yu proclaimed: "The autumn grain is ripening—the common people must not harvest it; all of it is for the army. I will not return until the bandits are pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Yu proclaimed publicly, "The autumn grain is ripening—the people are forbidden to harvest any of it; everything goes to the army. I will not return until the rebels are crushed."

sentences.zh: 聞者大懼，曰：「大軍不去，吾曹皆將餒死。」

translations.literal: Those who heard this were greatly afraid and said: "If the great army does not leave, we shall all starve to death."
translations.idiomatic: When they heard this they were terrified and said, "If the army does not leave, we shall all starve."

sentences.zh: 其中壯士乃入賊營，與所親潛謀，斬其渠帥而降，餘黨皆散，玉追討，悉平之。

translations.literal: Among them the stalwart men then entered the rebel camp, conspired secretly with their intimates, beheaded the rebel chieftains and surrendered; the remaining factions all scattered; Yu pursued and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the bolder men infiltrated the rebel camp, plotted secretly with kin inside, killed the rebel chiefs, and came over; the rest fled and scattered; Yu pursued them and pacified the entire region.

sentences.zh: 劉武周將宋金剛進攻澮州，陷之，軍勢甚銳。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang advanced to attack Fen Prefecture, took it, and his army's momentum was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang advanced on Fen Prefecture, captured it, and his army's momentum grew fierce.

sentences.zh: 裴寂性怯，無將帥之略，唯發使駱驛，趣虞、泰二州收民入城堡，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was timid by nature and lacked a commander's stratagems; he only sent messengers in relays urging the two prefectures of Yu and Tai to gather the people into forts and burn their stored goods.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was timid by nature and knew nothing of generalship; he only dispatched relay after relay of messengers ordering the prefectures of Yu and Tai to herd the populace into fortified towns and burn their stored grain.

sentences.zh: 民驚擾悉怨，皆思為盜。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed and disturbed, all resentful, and everyone turned his mind to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: The populace was thrown into panic and bitterness; everywhere men turned to brigandage.

sentences.zh: 夏縣民呂崇茂聚眾自稱魏王，以應武周，寂討之，為所敗。
