translations.literal: Lü Chongmao of Xia county gathered a host, styled himself King of Wei, and joined Wuzhou; Ji campaigned against him and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chongmao of Xia county raised a band, proclaimed himself King of Wei, and rallied to Wuzhou; Pei Ji marched against him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔永安王孝基、工部尚書獨孤懷恩、陝州總管於筠、內史侍郎唐儉等將兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en, regional commander of Shan Yu Jun, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian, and others to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince of Yong'an Li Xiaoji, Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en, Shan commander Yu Jun, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian, and others to take the field against him.

sentences.zh: 時王行本猶據蒲板，未下，亦與武周相應，關中震駭。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xingben still held Puban and had not fallen; he too coordinated with Wuzhou, and Guanzhong was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingben still held Puban, undefeated, and coordinated with Wuzhou as well; all of Guanzhong trembled with alarm.

sentences.zh: 上出手敕曰：「賊勢如此，難與爭鋒，宜棄大河以東，謹守關西而已。」

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a handwritten edict: "The bandit strength is such that it is hard to contend with their spearhead; we ought to abandon everything east of the Great River and merely hold Guanxi."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a personal edict: "The enemy is too strong to meet head-on; we should abandon everything east of the Yellow River and hold only the western passes."

sentences.zh: 秦王世民上表曰：「太原，王業所基，國之根本；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin Li Shimin submitted a memorial saying: "Taiyuan is the foundation of our royal enterprise, the root of the state;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, submitted a memorial: "Taiyuan is the foundation of our royal enterprise, the root of the realm;

sentences.zh: 河東殷實，京邑所資，若舉而棄之，臣竊憤恨。

translations.literal: Hedong is rich and solid, the capital's resource—if we raise it up only to cast it away, your servant inwardly burns with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong is prosperous and supplies the capital; to surrender it fills me with bitter outrage.

sentences.zh: 願假臣精兵三萬，必冀平殄武周，克復汾、晉。」

translations.literal: I beg to be lent thirty thousand elite troops; I surely hope to extinguish Wuzhou and recover Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me thirty thousand picked troops, and I am confident I can destroy Wuzhou and recover Fen and Jin."

sentences.zh: 上於是悉發關中兵以益世民所統，使擊武周，乙卯，幸華陰，至長春宮以送之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon sent out all the Guanzhong troops to augment Shimin's command and had him strike Wuzhou; on day Yimou he proceeded to Huayin, reaching Changchun Palace to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent every available soldier in Guanzhong to reinforce Shimin's command and dispatched him against Wuzhou; on the day Yimou he traveled to Huayin and went as far as Changchun Palace to see him off.

sentences.zh: 竇建德引兵趣衛州。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande led his army toward Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande marched his army toward Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建德每行軍，常為三道，輜重、細弱居中央，步騎夾左右，相去二里許。

translations.literal: Whenever Jiande marched he customarily formed three columns: baggage, women, and the weak in the center, infantry and cavalry flanking left and right, about two li apart.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign Jiande customarily marched in three columns: baggage, women, and noncombatants in the center, with infantry and cavalry on either flank, each column some two li apart.

sentences.zh: 建德以千騎前行，過黎陽三十里，李世勣遣騎將丘孝剛將二百騎偵之。

translations.literal: Jiande rode forward with a thousand horses, passing thirty li beyond Liyang; Li Shiji sent the cavalry officer Qiu Xiaogang with two hundred horsemen to scout him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande rode ahead with a thousand cavalry, passing thirty li beyond Liyang; Li Shiji sent cavalry commander Qiu Xiaogang with two hundred horsemen to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 孝剛驍勇，善馬槊，與建德遇，遂擊之，建德敗走；

translations.literal: Xiaogang was fierce and brave, skilled with the horse lance; he encountered Jiande and at once attacked; Jiande was defeated and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogang was famed for valor and mastery of the mounted lance; he met Jiande head-on and attacked; Jiande broke and fled;

sentences.zh: 右方兵救之，擊斬孝剛。

translations.literal: the right column came to the rescue and struck, killing Xiaogang.
translations.idiomatic: but the right column came up in relief, struck back, and killed Xiaogang.

sentences.zh: 建德怒，還攻黎陽，克之，虜淮安王神通、李世勣父蓋、魏徵及帝妹同安公主。

translations.literal: Jiande was furious, turned back to attack Liyang, took it, and captured Prince of Huai'an Shentong, Li Shiji's father Li Gai, Wei Zheng, and the Emperor's sister Princess Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jiande wheeled back on Liyang, took the city, and captured Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, Li Shiji's father Li Gai, Wei Zheng, and the Emperor's sister, Princess Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 唯李世勣以數百騎走渡河，數日，以其父故，還詣建德降。

translations.literal: Only Li Shiji with several hundred horsemen fled across the river; after several days, for his father's sake, he returned to Jiande and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji alone escaped across the river with a few hundred horsemen; within days, for his father's sake, he returned and surrendered to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 衛州聞黎陽陷，亦降。

translations.literal: Wei Prefecture heard that Liyang had fallen and also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Liyang had fallen, Wei Prefecture surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 建德以李世勣為左驍衛將軍，使守黎陽，常以其父蓋自隨為質。

translations.literal: Jiande made Li Shiji general of the Left Majestic Cavalry Guards, had him hold Liyang, and regularly kept his father Li Gai with him as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande appointed Li Shiji general of the Left Majestic Cavalry Guards and left him to hold Liyang, keeping Li Gai with his own army as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 以魏徵為起居舍人。

translations.literal: He made Wei Zheng attendant of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wei Zheng attendant of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 滑州刺史王軌奴殺軌，攜其首詣建德降。

translations.literal: The slave of Hua Prefecture governor Wang Gui killed Gui, carried his head, and came to Jiande to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A slave of Hua Prefecture governor Wang Gui murdered his master, took his head, and came to surrender to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「奴殺主大逆，吾何為受之！」

translations.literal: Jiande said: "For a slave to kill his master is the greatest treason—why should I accept him!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said, "A slave who murders his master commits the gravest of crimes—why would I accept such a man!"

sentences.zh: 立命斬奴，返其首於滑州。

translations.literal: He at once ordered the slave executed and returned the head to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had the slave executed and sent the head back to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吏民感悅，即日請降。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners were moved and pleased, and that same day asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people were deeply moved; that very day they asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是其旁州縣及徐圓朗等皆望風歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the neighboring prefectures and counties and men such as Xu Yuanlang all joined him at the mere sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon neighboring prefectures and counties, and warlords such as Xu Yuanlang, submitted at the mere rumor of his approach.

sentences.zh: 己未，建德還洺州，築萬春宮，徙都之。

translations.literal: On day Jiwei Jiande returned to Ming Prefecture, built the Palace of Ten Thousand Springs, and moved his capital there.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiwei, Jiande returned to Ming Prefecture, built the Palace of Ten Thousand Springs, and transferred his capital there.

sentences.zh: 置淮安王神通於下博，待以客禮。

translations.literal: He placed Prince of Huai'an Shentong at Xiabo and received him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong at Xiabo and treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管羅士信帥勇士夜入洛陽外郭，縱火焚清化裡而還。

translations.literal: Campaign general Luo Shixin led warriors by night into the outer wards of Luoyang, set fire burning Qinghua ward, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign general Luo Shixin led picked warriors in a night raid on Luoyang's outer wards, set Qinghua Lane ablaze, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，士信拔青城堡。

translations.literal: On day Renxu Shixin captured Qingcheng fort.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renxu, Shixin captured Qingcheng fort.

sentences.zh: 王世充自將兵徇地至滑台，臨黎陽；

translations.literal: Wang Shichong personally led troops to tour the territory as far as Huatai, drawing near Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong personally led an army on a sweep of the region as far as Huatai, pressing up to Liyang;

sentences.zh: 尉氏城主時德睿、汴州刺史王要漢、亳州刺史丁叔則遣使降之。

translations.literal: Weishi city chief Shi Derui, Bian Prefecture governor Wang Yaohan, and Bo Prefecture governor Ding Shuzhe each sent envoys to surrender to him.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi's chief Shi Derui, Bian Prefecture governor Wang Yaohan, and Bo Prefecture governor Ding Shuzhe each sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 以德睿為尉州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Derui governor of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong appointed Derui governor of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 要漢，伯當之兄也。

translations.literal: Yaohan was the elder brother of Bo Dangang.
translations.idiomatic: Yaohan was the elder brother of Bo Dangang.

sentences.zh: 夏侯端至黎陽，李世勣發兵送之，自澶淵濟河，傳檄州縣，東至於海，南至於淮，二十餘州，皆遣使來降。

translations.literal: Xiahou Duan reached Liyang; Li Shiji sent troops to escort him; he crossed the river from Chanyuan, issued proclamations to prefectures and counties—from the sea in the east to the Huai in the south, more than twenty prefectures—all sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Duan reached Liyang, where Li Shiji dispatched troops to escort him; he crossed the Yellow River at Chanyuan and issued proclamations to the counties. From the sea in the east to the Huai in the south, more than twenty prefectures sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 行至譙州，會汴、亳降於王世充，還路遂絕。

translations.literal: When he reached Qiao Prefecture, Bian and Bo had surrendered to Wang Shichong, and his return route was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Qiao Prefecture, Bian and Bo had gone over to Wang Shichong, and his path home was cut off.

sentences.zh: 端素得眾心，所從二千人，雖糧盡不忍委去，端坐澤中，殺馬以饗士，因歔欷謂曰：「卿等鄉里皆已從賊，特以共事之情，未能見委。

translations.literal: Duan had long won men's hearts; the two thousand who followed him, though provisions were exhausted, could not bear to abandon him. He sat upright in the marshland, slaughtered horses to feast the troops, and sighing said: "Your home districts have all joined the bandits; it is only because we have served together that you have not yet forsaken me.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had always won the loyalty of those under him; though provisions were gone, the two thousand who followed him would not leave him. He sat in the midst of the marsh, slaughtered his horses to feed his men, and with tears said, "Your homelands have all gone over to the rebels. It is only our bond as comrades that keeps you from abandoning me.

sentences.zh: 我奉王命，不可從卿；

translations.literal: I bear the king's commission—I cannot follow you;
translations.idiomatic: I hold the Son of Heaven's commission—I cannot follow you;

sentences.zh: 卿有妻子，無宜效我。

translations.literal: you have wives and children—you ought not to imitate me.
translations.idiomatic: you have wives and children—you ought not to die with me.

sentences.zh: 可斬吾首歸賊，必獲富貴。」

translations.literal: You may cut off my head and return to the bandits—you will surely win wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Cut off my head and surrender to the enemy—you are sure to win wealth and honors."

sentences.zh: 眾皆流涕曰：「公於唐室非有親屬，直以忠義，志不圖存。

translations.literal: All wept and said: "My lord has no kinship with the house of Tang—you uphold loyalty and righteousness alone, with no thought of saving your own life.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and said, "My lord has no kin tie to the house of Tang—you live only by loyalty and righteousness, with no thought for your own survival.

sentences.zh: 某等雖賤，心亦人也，寧肯害公以求利乎！」

translations.literal: We may be base, yet our hearts are human too—how could we harm my lord to seek profit!"
translations.idiomatic: We may be humble men, but we are human still—how could we harm you for gain!"

sentences.zh: 端曰：「卿不忍見殺，吾當自刎。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "Since you cannot bear to kill me, I shall take my own life with a sword."
translations.idiomatic: Duan said, "Since you will not kill me, I shall fall on my sword."

sentences.zh: 眾抱持之，乃復同進，潛行五日，餒死及為賊所擊奔潰相失者太半，唯餘五十三人同走，采豆生食之。

translations.literal: The crowd seized and held him; they then advanced together again, traveling stealthily for five days; of those who died of hunger or were scattered when struck by bandits, more than half were lost—only fifty-three remained to flee together, gathering beans in the wild and eating them raw.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him and would not let go. Together they pressed on in secret for five days; more than half perished of hunger or were scattered in enemy attacks—only fifty-three remained, gathering wild beans and eating them raw.

sentences.zh: 端持節未嘗離身，屢遣從者散，自求生，眾又不可。

translations.literal: Duan held his credentials of office and never let them leave his person; repeatedly he urged his followers to scatter and save themselves—the crowd would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Duan never let his credentials of office leave his person. Again and again he urged his followers to disperse and save themselves; they would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 時河南之地皆入世充，唯杞州刺史李公逸為唐堅守，遣兵迎端，館給之。

translations.literal: At that time all the lands of Henan had entered Shichong's realm; only Qi Prefecture governor Li Gongyi held firm for Tang, sent troops to welcome Duan, and lodged and supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: By then all Henan had fallen to Shichong; only Qi Prefecture governor Li Gongyi still held for Tang, sent troops to welcome Duan, and provided him lodging and supplies.

sentences.zh: 世充遣使召端，解衣遺之，仍送除書，以端為淮南郡公、尚書少吏部。

translations.literal: Shichong sent envoys to summon Duan, presented him with clothing stripped from his own person, and also sent a letter of appointment making Duan Duke of Huainan commandery and Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent envoys to summon him, gifted him with garments from his own wardrobe, and sent a commission appointing Duan Duke of Huainan and Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 端對使者焚書毀衣，曰：「夏侯端天子大使，豈受王世充官乎！

translations.literal: Duan faced the envoys, burned the commission and destroyed the clothes, and said: "Xiahou Duan is the Son of Heaven's ambassador—how could I accept office from Wang Shichong!
translations.idiomatic: Duan burned the commission and tore up the gifts before the envoys and said, "Xiahou Duan is an ambassador of the Son of Heaven—how could I accept office from Wang Shichong!

sentences.zh: 汝欲吾往，唯可取吾首耳。」

translations.literal: If you wish me to go, you may take only my head."
translations.idiomatic: If you want me to come, you may have only my head."

sentences.zh: 因解節旄懷之，置刃於竿，自山中西走，無復蹊徑，冒踐荊棘，晝夜兼行，得達宜陽，從者附崖溺水，為虎狼所食，又喪其半；

translations.literal: Thereupon he removed the standard streamers, clasped them to his breast, set a blade on the staff, and fled westward through the mountains where paths no longer existed, forcing his way through thorns and brambles, traveling day and night without rest until he reached Yiyang; followers fell from cliffs and drowned, were devoured by tigers and wolves, and half were lost again;
translations.idiomatic: He took down his ceremonial staff, clasped its insignia to his breast, fixed a blade to the pole, and fled west through the mountains along paths that were no path at all, forcing his way through bramble and thorn, traveling without rest by day or night until he reached Yiyang. Followers plunged from cliffs and drowned or were torn apart by wolves and tigers; half his company was lost again.

sentences.zh: 其存者鬢髮禿落，無復人狀。

translations.literal: Those who survived had hair and whiskers fallen out, no longer in human form.
translations.idiomatic: Those who survived had hair fallen out and bodies wasted until they scarcely looked human.

sentences.zh: 端詣闕見上，但謝無功，初不自言艱苦，上復以為秘書監。

translations.literal: Duan went to court to see the Emperor, thanked him only for having achieved nothing, and at first did not speak of his hardships; the Emperor again appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Duan presented himself at court. He offered only apologies for his failure and never spoke of what he had endured; the Emperor reappointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 郎楚之至山東，亦為竇建德所獲，楚之不屈，竟得還。

translations.literal: When Lang Chuzhi reached Shandong he too was captured by Dou Jiande. Chuzhi would not submit and in the end was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang Chuzhi reached Shandong he too was taken by Dou Jiande. Chuzhi refused to yield and was eventually allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 王世充遣其從弟世辯以徐、亳之兵攻雍丘。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent his younger cousin Shibian with the armies of Xu and Bo to attack Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his cousin Shibian with troops from Xu and Bo to attack Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 李公逸遣使求救，上以隔賊境，不能救。

translations.literal: Li Gongyi sent envoys begging for rescue, but the emperor said that because enemy territory lay between them he could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongyi sent envoys pleading for help, but the emperor said enemy-held territory lay between them and he could not send relief.

sentences.zh: 公逸乃留其屬李善行守雍丘，身帥輕騎入朝，至襄城，為世充伊州刺史張殷所獲。

translations.literal: Gongyi then left his follower Li Shanxing to defend Yongqiu and personally led light cavalry to court. When he reached Xiangcheng he was captured by Zhang Yin, Shichong's governor of Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi left his follower Li Shanxing to hold Yongqiu and rode to court with a light escort. At Xiangcheng he was captured by Zhang Yin, Shichong's governor of Yi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世充謂曰：「卿越鄭臣唐，其說安在？」

translations.literal: Shichong said to him: 'You crossed from Zheng to serve Tang—what is your explanation?'
translations.idiomatic: Shichong asked him: 'You abandoned Zheng to serve Tang—how do you justify that?'

sentences.zh: 公逸曰：「我於天下，唯知有唐，不知有鄭。」

translations.literal: Gongyi said: 'In all the realm I know only Tang; I do not know Zheng.'
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi replied: 'In all the realm I acknowledge only Tang—I know nothing of Zheng.'

sentences.zh: 世充怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Shichong was angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong flew into a rage and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 善行亦沒。

translations.literal: Shanxing also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxing was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 上以公逸子為襄邑公。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed Gongyi's son as Duke of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed Gongyi's son as Duke of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上祠華山。

translations.literal: On day Jiazi the emperor offered sacrifice at Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi the emperor performed sacrifice at Mount Hua.
